title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上御極之四年爲萬曆丙子復
當鄉試之期秋七月五日
上命〔臣洵臣思育〕往典應天府試
事翌日
陛辭乘傳行以八月六日至應
天府入院時府尹〔臣嗣功〕府
===
丞〔臣樹德〕御史〔臣堂臣秉性〕
及例增御史〔臣林應訓臣于
應昌〕相與飭防儲具甚備乃
進提學御史〔臣褚鈇〕及諸曹
館所選士凡四千四百餘人
三試之而與同考試官推官
〔臣元熙〕教授〔臣一桂〕教諭〔臣〕
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上御極之四年，爲萬曆丙子，復當鄉試之期。秋七月五日，上命〔臣洵、臣思育〕往典應天府試事。翌日陛辭，乘傳行，以八月六日至應天府入院。時府尹〔臣嗣功〕、府丞〔臣樹德〕、御史〔臣堂、臣秉性〕及例增御史〔臣林應訓、臣于應昌〕相與飭防儲具甚備。乃進提學御史〔臣褚鈇〕及諸曹館所選士，凡四千四百餘人，三試之。而與同考試官推官〔臣元熙〕、教授〔臣一桂〕、教諭〔臣〕
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination

In the fourth year of His Majesty's reign, the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), the time for the Provincial Examination came round once more. On the fifth day of the seventh month in autumn, the Emperor commanded your servants Xun 洵 and Siyu 思育 to go and take charge of the examination affairs of Yingtian Prefecture. The following day, having taken leave of the throne, we traveled by post relay, arriving at Yingtian Prefecture and entering the examination compound on the sixth day of the eighth month.

At that time, the Prefect of Yingtian, your servant Sigong 嗣功; the Vice Prefect, your servant Shude 樹德; the Censors, your servants Tang 堂 and Bingxing 秉性; as well as the Censors added by precedent, your servants Lin Yingxun 林應訓 and Yu Yingchang 于應昌, had together put the security measures in order and prepared the supplies very thoroughly. We thereupon admitted the candidates selected by the Education-intendant Censor, your servant Chu Fu 褚鈇, and by the various agencies and Directorate of Education—totaling more than four thousand four hundred men—and examined them in three sessions. Together with the Associate Examiners—the Prefectural Judge, your servant Yuanxi 元熙; the Prefectural Director of Studies, your servant Yigui 一桂; the County Directors of Studies, your servants …

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
來賓臣佑臣譽臣資瀾臣伯
椿臣一清臣養賢臣守廉臣
維翰等謹校閱得百三十五
人將錄其文以
獻臣宜叙諸首簡臣竊惟
國家設科取士將以藉其用也
取士而試之文欲驗所學以
===
得其可用之實也故士非可
用者勿學非素所學者勿言
居學之應試而言之臨事任
而用之若合質劵然有必不
可爽者記曰事君先資其言
拜自獻其身以成其信故士
之應試也亦士之先資他日
punctuated: 來賓、臣佑、臣譽、臣資瀾、臣伯椿、臣一清、臣養賢、臣守廉、臣維翰等，謹校閱，得百三十五人。將錄其文以獻，臣宜叙諸首簡。臣竊惟國家設科取士，將以藉其用也；取士而試之文，欲驗所學以得其可用之實也。故士非可用者勿學，非素所學者勿言。居學之，應試而言之，臨事任而用之，若合質劵然，有必不可爽者。《記》曰：「事君先資其言，拜自獻其身，以成其信。」故士之應試也，亦士之先資，他日
translation_en:
… Laibin 來賓, Your Servant You 佑, Your Servant Yu 譽, Your Servant Zilan 資瀾, Your Servant Bochun 伯椿, Your Servant Yiqing 一清, Your Servant Yangxian 養賢, Your Servant Shoulian 守廉, Your Servant Weihan 維翰, and others—carefully read and evaluated the papers, selecting one hundred and thirty-five men. As we are about to print their essays for presentation to the Throne, it is fitting that Your Servant write a preface for the opening pages.

Your Servant humbly reflects that when the State establishes examination categories to select scholars, it intends to rely on their practical service; and when it selects scholars by testing them with literary compositions, it seeks to verify what they have learned in order to obtain the reality of their usefulness. Therefore, scholars should not study what cannot be put to use, nor should they speak of what they have not habitually studied. What they study in private life, they express in words when sitting for the examinations, and they put into practice when taking on official duties and responsibilities—just like matching the two halves of a tally or contract, which must never fail to correspond. The Record of Rites (Liji) says: "In serving a ruler, one first presents one's words as a pledge, and then bows to offer one's person in order to fulfill the trust in those words." Thus, when a scholar sits for the examinations, this too is the scholar's initial pledge, which on a future day…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
所考成而取信者也應天我
國家興王地淑氣所鍾獨爲深
厚士以實學用於世者後先
相望乃至於今而文章號爲
極盛矣文日盛則實漸微學
不務其實而競於奇則其用
有不必根於學而其言有不
===
必適於用者然則將安所成
其信哉市井細人之相要約
也一不售猶且羞之設令以
市井命士則怫然怒矣顧恬
然習謾不思售莫以爲怪此
識者所爲慮也臣自受
命以來日夕思所少回士習不宜
punctuated: 所考成而取信者也。應天，我國家興王地，淑氣所鍾，獨爲深厚，士以實學用於世者，後先相望；乃至於今，而文章號爲極盛矣。文日盛則實漸微，學不務其實而競於奇，則其用有不必根於學，而其言有不必適於用者。然則將安所成其信哉？市井細人之相要約也，一不售，猶且羞之。設令以市井命士，則怫然怒矣；顧恬然習謾不思售，莫以爲怪，此識者所爲慮也。臣自受命以來，日夕思所少回士習，不宜
translation_en: …by which their achievements will be evaluated and their trustworthiness proven. Yingtian is the foundational homeland of our dynasty, where the finest vital energies gather in uniquely deep abundance. Scholars who applied practical learning to the service of the world have followed one after another in unbroken succession; yet by the present day, literary refinement is acclaimed as having reached its absolute zenith. As literary flourish grows daily more flourishing, substance gradually wanes. When scholars do not devote their learning to substance but compete in novelty, then their practical application is not necessarily rooted in their learning, and their words are not necessarily suited to practical application. If that is so, how then will they establish their trustworthiness? When petty folk of the marketplace make agreements with one another, if even once they fail to make good on their word, they still feel ashamed of it. Suppose one were to call a scholar a marketplace peddler—he would bristle in anger. Yet scholars calmly accustom themselves to empty deception without giving a thought to making good on their words, and no one regards this as strange. This is what worries men of discernment. Ever since your servant received his commission, day and night I have pondered how to somewhat restore the habits of the scholars: that one ought not…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
先示好奇之端諸所命題皆
明白正大不復摘抉隱僻以
難諸士而諸所取士必根理
要中典則其有不本經術或
稱引諸百氏家艱深語以見
其奇者悉棄不取蓋心正則
其言簡以重心誠則其言切
===
以醇嘐玄虛者荒其思盛藻
續者淫其志此自然之徵有
非誣者若苟見言語之奇而
取之庸悅一時之耳目則可
耳非所以任
國家之重也〔臣〕爲
國家取士而以苟悅耳目者充
punctuated: 先示好奇之端，諸所命題皆明白正大，不復摘抉隱僻以難諸士；而諸所取士，必根理要、中典則。其有不本經術，或稱引諸百氏家艱深語以見其奇者，悉棄不取。蓋心正則其言簡以重，心誠則其言切以醇；嘐玄虛者荒其思，盛藻續者淫其志，此自然之徵，有非誣者。若苟見言語之奇而取之，庸悅一時之耳目則可耳，非所以任國家之重也。〔臣〕爲國家取士，而以苟悅耳目者充
translation_en: …first display any sign of a fondness for novelty. All the examination topics that were set were clear, straightforward, and upright, no longer picking out obscure and abstruse passages to stump the candidates; and all the scholars whom we selected had to be grounded in essential principles and conform to canonical standards. Those whose writings were not rooted in classical learning, or who quoted abstruse language from the various Hundred Schools in order to show off their novelty, were all rejected and not selected. For when the mind is upright, one's words are concise and weighty; when the mind is sincere, one's words are pertinent and pure. Those who boast of mysterious emptiness let their thoughts run wild, and those who pile up florid embellishments [?] corrupt their aims—these are natural manifestations that cannot be falsified. If one were carelessly to select candidates merely on seeing novelty in their language, that might suffice to please the eyes and ears of the moment, yet it is not the way to bear the heavy responsibilities of the state. Your servant selects scholars for the state; if I were to fill the ranks with those who merely please the eyes and ears…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之臣之罪可逭哉此臣之愚
所以寧取此不取彼也雖然
論篤是與聖人戒焉其或言
若近正而實則鹵莽於身心
濶踈於措置者亦豈無哉以
此用之則闒茸頹靡其不能
取效將反爲衒奇者所咲此
===
允臣之所慮也而非臣之所
能逆覩也夫庸者用則事不
舉而奇者用則事壞與其壞
也無寧不舉也此在上用士
者之慮也若士惟假諸言以
干進既進而卽委之若土苴
焉則雖原本於經術與譁鶩
punctuated: 之，臣之罪可逭哉？此臣之愚所以寧取此不取彼也。雖然，「論篤是與」，聖人戒焉。其或言若近正，而實則鹵莽於身心、濶踈於措置者，亦豈無哉？以此用之，則闒茸頹靡，其不能取效，將反爲衒奇者所咲。此允臣之所慮也，而非臣之所能逆覩也。夫庸者用則事不舉，而奇者用則事壞；與其壞也，無寧不舉也。此在上用士者之慮也。若士惟假諸言以干進，既進而卽委之若土苴焉，則雖原本於經術，與譁鶩
translation_en: … the ranks with them, how could your servant escape blame for such a transgression? This is why your foolish servant would rather select the former and reject the latter. Even so, the Sage warned against "endorsing a man simply because his words sound earnest." How could there not also be those whose words seem close to orthodoxy, yet who in reality are careless in personal cultivation and impractical in managing affairs? If such men are employed on this basis, they will prove mediocre and listless; their inability to achieve results will instead make them a laughingstock to those who peddle novelty. This is truly what your servant worries about [Note: reading 允 as 尤, "especially", or "truly"], yet it is not something your servant can foresee in advance. Now, when mediocre men are employed, affairs go unaccomplished; when eccentric men are employed, affairs are ruined. Rather than having affairs ruined, it is better that they go unaccomplished. This is the concern of those above who employ scholars. As for the scholars themselves, if they merely borrow such words to seek advancement, and once advanced immediately cast them aside like dirt and straw, then even if their essays were grounded in canonical learning, compared with those who clamorously chase after…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
於百家者其爲自欺且欺上
則等耳此非士所當自爲慮
哉士不苟言要以適用士不
苟用要以酬君今
聖天子作新天下方崇責實之效
諸士今日之文固質券也他
日將必於爾乎取償焉雖欲
===
復爲謾也得乎哉爾多士其
熟慮之毋終爲負券之夫也
左春坊左中允兼翰林院編
修戴洵謹序
punctuated:
於百家者，其爲自欺且欺上則等耳。此非士所當自爲慮哉？士不苟言，要以適用；士不苟用，要以酬君。今聖天子作新天下，方崇責實之效，諸士今日之文，固質券也。他日將必於爾乎取償焉，雖欲復爲謾也，得乎哉？爾多士其熟慮之，毋終爲負券之夫也。
左春坊左中允兼翰林院編修戴洵謹序。
translation_en:
…among the Hundred Schools, they are equal in deceiving both themselves and their superiors. Is this not what scholars ought to take thought for on their own account? A scholar does not speak carelessly—the essential point is to be suited to practical application; a scholar does not accept employment carelessly—the essential point is to repay his sovereign. Now the Sacred Son of Heaven is renewing All under Heaven and is at this very moment exalting the efficacy of demanding actual substance. The essays written by you scholars today are indeed pledges and tally-contracts. On another day, redemption will surely be exacted from you; even if you should wish to engage in empty deception again, could you succeed in doing so? May all you scholars ponder this thoroughly, and do not in the end become men who default on their pledges.

Respectfully prefaced by Dai Xun 戴洵, Left Companion of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and Concurrently Historiographer of the Hanlin Academy.

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:

監試官
文林郎南京湖廣道監察御史陳　堂〔明佐廣東南海縣籍 番禺縣人戊辰進士〕
文林郎南京山東道監察御史胡秉性〔汝成河南信陽州人 辛酉貢士〕
收掌試卷官
奉議大夫應天府治中黃喬棟〔以藩福建晉江縣人 官生〕
印卷官
應　天　府　通　判秦致恭〔幸禮廣西靈川縣人 戊辰進士〕
承務郎應天府推官詹世用〔汝賓江西弋陽縣人 戊辰進士〕
受卷官
直隸鳳陽府推官王致祥〔德徵萬全都司籍山 西忻州人辛未進士〕
直隸太平府推官劉　垓〔達可湖廣潛江縣籍江 西安福縣人辛未進士〕
直隸安慶府推官葉　遵〔子憲浙江餘姚縣人 甲戌進士〕
彌封官
承直郎應天府上元縣知縣林大黼〔朝介福建莆田縣人 壬子貢士〕
直隸廬州府合肥縣知縣胡時化〔惟推浙江餘姚縣人 辛未進士〕
直隸鎮江府丹陽縣知縣尹良任〔志伊湖廣漢川縣人 辛未進士〕
謄錄官
punctuated:
四川夔州府雲陽縣儒學教諭伍維翰〔宗卿，貴州安莊衛人，西臨桂縣人，丁卯貢士〕。

監試官：
文林郎、南京湖廣道監察御史陳堂〔明佐，廣東南海縣籍，番禺縣人，戊辰進士〕；
文林郎、南京山東道監察御史胡秉性〔汝成，河南信陽州人，辛酉貢士〕。

收掌試卷官：
奉議大夫、應天府治中黃喬棟〔以藩，福建晉江縣人，官生〕。

印卷官：
應天府通判秦致恭〔幸禮，廣西靈川縣人，戊辰進士〕；
承務郎、應天府推官詹世用〔汝賓，江西弋陽縣人，戊辰進士〕。

受卷官：
直隸鳳陽府推官王致祥〔德徵，萬全都司籍，山西忻州人，辛未進士〕；
直隸太平府推官劉垓〔達可，湖廣潛江縣籍，江西安福縣人，辛未進士〕；
直隸安慶府推官葉遵〔子憲，浙江餘姚縣人，甲戌進士〕。

彌封官：
承直郎、應天府上元縣知縣林大黼〔朝介，福建莆田縣人，壬子貢士〕；
直隸廬州府合肥縣知縣胡時化〔惟推，浙江餘姚縣人，辛未進士〕；
直隸鎮江府丹陽縣知縣尹良任〔志伊，湖廣漢川縣人，辛未進士〕。

謄錄官：

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰道千乘之國敬事而節用而信愛人
使民以時
誠者自成也而道自道也誠者物之終始
不誠無物是故君子誠之爲貴誠者非
自成已而已也所以成物也成已仁也
成物知也性之德也合外內之道也故
時措之宜也
===
舉舜而敷治焉舜使益掌火益烈山澤而
焚之禽獸逃匿禹疏九河瀹濟漯而注
諸海決汝漢排淮泗而注之江然後中
國可得而食也當是時也禹八年於外
三過其門而不入雖欲耕得乎后稷教
民稼穡樹藝五穀五穀熟而民人育人
之有道也飽食煖衣逸居而無教則近
於禽獸聖人有憂之使契爲司徒教以
人倫父子有親君臣有義夫婦有別長
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

子曰：「道千乘之國，敬事而節用，而信，愛人，使民以時。」

誠者，自成也；而道，自道也。誠者，物之終始；不誠，無物。是故君子誠之爲貴。誠者，非自成已而已也，所以成物也。成已，仁也；成物，知也。性之德也，合外內之道也，故時措之宜也。

舉舜而敷治焉。舜使益掌火，益烈山澤而焚之，禽獸逃匿。禹疏九河，瀹濟漯而注諸海，決汝漢，排淮泗而注之江，然後中國可得而食也。當是時也，禹八年於外，三過其門而不入，雖欲耕，得乎？后稷教民稼穡，樹藝五穀，五穀熟而民人育。人之有道也，飽食、煖衣、逸居而無教，則近於禽獸。聖人有憂之，使契爲司徒，教以人倫：父子有親，君臣有義，夫婦有別，長…
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books

The Master said: "In guiding a state of a thousand chariots, attend reverently to affairs and be frugal in expenditure, and be trustworthy [? text transposes 'be trustworthy' and 'be frugal in expenditure' from the standard Analects 1.5], love the people, and employ the populace only at the proper seasons."

Sincerity is self-completion, and the Way is self-direction. Sincerity is the beginning and end of things; without sincerity, there would be nothing. Therefore, the noble man regards the attainment of sincerity as precious. Sincerity is not merely the completion of oneself; it is that by which one completes other things as well. Completing oneself is humaneness (ren); completing other things is wisdom (zhi). These are the virtues of one's nature, and the Way of uniting the outer and the inner; therefore, whenever it is applied, it is fitting.

[Yao] raised up Shun to spread governance everywhere. Shun appointed Yi to take charge of fire, and Yi set fire to the mountains and marshes and burned them, so that the birds and beasts fled and hid. Yu dredged the Nine Rivers, cleared the Ji and Ta rivers and channeled them into the sea, opened up the Ru and Han rivers, and cleared away the obstructions of the Huai and Si rivers to channel them into the Yangzi. Only after this could the Central Land obtain food to eat. At that time, Yu spent eight years away from home, passing the door of his own house three times without entering—even if he had wished to plow the fields himself, could he have done so? Hou Ji taught the people to sow and reap, and to cultivate the five grains; when the five grains ripened, the people were nourished. As for the Way of human beings: if they eat their fill, wear warm clothes, and live in comfort, yet lack instruction, they come close to the birds and beasts. The Sage was worried about this, and so he appointed Xie to be Minister of Education (situ), to teach them the human relationships: that between father and son there should be affection, between ruler and minister there should be righteousness, between husband and wife there should be distinction, between elder and…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
幼有序朋友有信放勳曰勞之來之匡
之直之輔之翼之使自得之又從而振
德之聖人之憂民如此而暇耕乎堯以
不得舜爲已憂舜以不得禹臯陶爲已
憂夫以百畝之不易爲已憂者農夫也
易
安貞之吉應地无疆
天地相遇品物咸章也剛遇中正天下大
行也
===
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深也
故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成天下
之務唯神也故不疾而速不行而至子
曰易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
象也者像此者也
書
一日二日萬幾
非知之艱行之惟艱王忱不艱允協于先
王成德惟說不言有厥咎
punctuated:
幼有序，朋友有信。放勳曰：「勞之來之，匡之直之，輔之翼之，使自得之，又從而振德之。」聖人之憂民如此，而暇耕乎？堯以不得舜爲已憂，舜以不得禹、臯陶爲已憂。夫以百畝之不易爲已憂者，農夫也。

易：
「安貞之吉，應地无疆。」
「天地相遇，品物咸章也。剛遇中正，天下大行也。」
「夫《易》，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。子曰『《易》有聖人之道四焉』者，此之謂也。」
「象也者，像此者也。」

書：
「一日二日萬幾。」
「非知之艱，行之惟艱。王忱不艱，允協于先王成德；惟說不言，有厥咎。」
translation_en:
…between elder and younger there is proper order, and between friends there is good faith. Fangxun [Yao] said: 'Encourage them and lead them on; rectify them and straighten them; assist them and give them wings, so as to make them attain it for themselves, and then further stimulate them and confer kindness upon them.' When the sages' anxiety for the people was like this, did they have leisure to plow? Yao took not finding Shun as his own anxiety; Shun took not finding Yu and Gao Yao as his own anxiety. Now, he who takes the failure to cultivate his hundred mu of land as his own anxiety is a mere farmer."

Book of Changes (Yi):
"The good fortune of peaceful constancy corresponds to the boundless capacity of the earth."
"When heaven and earth meet, all things in their categories become manifest. When the firm meets the central and correct, great is its prevalence throughout the world."
"Now, the Changes is that by which the sages plumb the utmost depths and investigate the subtle springs of things. Only because of its depth can it penetrate the wills of all under heaven; only because of its grasp of the subtle springs can it accomplish the affairs of all under heaven; only because it is spirit-like does it make haste without hurrying and arrive without traveling. When the Master said, 'The Changes has four ways of the sages,' this is what was meant."
"The images are what give likeness to this."

Book of Documents (Shu):
"In one day or two days there are ten thousand subtle springs of affairs."
"It is not knowing that is difficult, but acting that is difficult. Since the King's sincerity is not deterred by the difficulty, he will truly accord with the perfected virtue of the former king; if I, Yue, should fail to speak, the fault would be mine."

"Just as in working with catalpa wood, when one has diligently shaped and hewn it, one must then apply the red and green pigments."

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"Guan-guan cry the ospreys, on the islet in the river; delicate and virtuous is the maiden, a good match for the lord."
"Showing the people not to be frivolous, the gentlemen take him as their model and pattern."
"His armies were three single divisions; he measured the lowlands and plains, and assessed the fields under the mutual-share system for grain."
"How is it with the newly broken fields and the fields in their third year? Oh, glorious are the wheat and barley! Soon we shall receive their bright bounty."

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
夜禁
違令
第叄場
策五道
問古昔帝王之學動息有養盤盂几席皆
著箴銘心畫遺文亦略可紀自漢以下
英君慕古間摛藻翰而臣下時沾賚焉
有細書一劄十行以風吏治者有手墨
大字數函以勵將臣者或以飛白賜侍
臣而需舟楫之用者或以孝經易千文
而明教化之理者蓋皆流誦當時貽芳
來葉矣其果足爲勸戒否歟我
===
太祖高皇帝經綸草昧他未遑務也嘗揭大學
衍義於壁間書洪範九疇於座右又以
其暇
親製聯句以
賜諫臣賦楚辭以
賜侍臣
punctuated:
夜禁。
違令。

第叄場
策五道

問：古昔帝王之學，動息有養，盤盂几席，皆著箴銘，心畫遺文，亦略可紀。自漢以下，英君慕古，間摛藻翰，而臣下時沾賚焉。有細書一劄十行，以風吏治者；有手墨大字數函，以勵將臣者；或以飛白賜侍臣，而需舟楫之用者；或以《孝經》易《千文》，而明教化之理者。蓋皆流誦當時，貽芳來葉矣。其果足爲勸戒否歟？我太祖高皇帝經綸草昧，他未遑務也，嘗揭《大學衍義》於壁間，書《洪範》九疇於座右；又以其暇，親製聯句以賜諫臣，賦《楚辭》以賜侍臣。
translation_en:
Violation of Night Curfew.
Violation of Ordinances.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: In the learning of emperors and kings of antiquity, they cultivated themselves in both movement and rest, inscribing admonitions and mottoes upon their washbasins, bowls, low tables, and mats; these calligraphic traces of the mind and surviving texts can still be outlined in the record. From the Han dynasty onward, heroic rulers who admired antiquity occasionally spread forth ornate calligraphy and brushwork, and their subjects from time to time were favored with such gifts. There were those who wrote in fine script on a single tablet of ten lines in order to encourage good governance among officials; those who wrote large characters in their own hand across several cases to inspire military commanders; some who bestowed "flying white" (feibai) calligraphy upon attendant officials while looking to them for service as the "oars and boat" of state; and others who replaced the Thousand Character Classic (Qianwen) with the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) so as to clarify the principles of moral transformation. All of these were recited and circulated in their own day and left a fragrant reputation to future generations. Yet were they truly sufficient to serve as encouragement and admonition? When Our Taizu, Emperor Gao, was bringing order out of the initial chaos of founding the dynasty and had no leisure for other pursuits, he once posted the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) upon his walls and inscribed the Nine Categories of the "Great Plan" ("Hongfan") beside his seat; and in his spare moments, he personally composed linked verses to bestow upon remonstrance officials and composed lyrics in the style of the Songs of Chu (Chuci) to bestow upon attendant officials. …

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天文
睿藻照耀今古豈前代之所侔歟我
皇上冲齡英邁他無嗜好也嘗
親揭書序要語於
殿額書十二事當省戒者於
宮中又以其暇大書徑尺字以
賜輔臣
宸章
奎翰儷美
===
祖孫誠萬世之所希遘矣乃
心學之純又有出於藝文之外者爾諸士亦
能揚其休歟夫難究者學難持者心儻
更攄嘉謨爲
聖修助執事者固願采之以獻也
問古者設左右史以紀言動蓋以裨君德
而垂治鑑也所從來尚矣成周時金縢
史祝雖畢召不得與聞蓋其密也後世
廼有每月奏御者有欲當朝顯言其狀
punctuated:
天文睿藻，照耀今古，豈前代之所侔歟？我皇上冲齡英邁，他無嗜好也。嘗親揭《書序》要語於殿額，書十二事當省戒者於宮中，又以其暇大書徑尺字以賜輔臣。宸章奎翰，儷美祖孫，誠萬世之所希遘矣。乃心學之純，又有出於藝文之外者，爾諸士亦能揚其休歟？夫難究者學，難持者心，儻更攄嘉謨為聖修助，執事者固願采之以獻也。

問：古者設左右史以紀言動，蓋以裨君德而垂治鑑也，所從來尚矣。成周時，金縢史祝，雖畢、召不得與聞，蓋其密也。後世廼有每月奏御者，有欲當朝顯言其狀，
translation_en:
…Heavenly writings and imperial compositions shine across past and present—how could any former dynasty compare with this? Our reigning Emperor, though young in years, is heroic and surpassing in spirit, having no other indulgences. He has personally posted essential maxims from the Prefaces to the Book of Documents (Shu xu) upon the palacelintel, inscribed inside the palace twelve matters calling for self-examination and caution, and in His leisure time written great characters a foot across to bestow upon the Grand Secretaries. Imperial writings and stellar brush-strokes match in splendor between Grandfather and Grandson—truly a rare encounter in ten thousand generations! Yet the purity of Their learning of the mind-and-heart reaches even beyond literary and calligraphic arts; can you gentlemen also extol its magnificence? Now, what is difficult to exhaust is learning, and what is difficult to hold fast is the mind-and-heart. Should you further set forth fine counsels to aid in Imperial self-cultivation, this official would certainly wish to gather them for presentation to the throne.

Question: In antiquity, Left and Right Scribes (Zuoyou shi) were established to record words and deeds, in order to aid the ruler's virtue and hand down a mirror for governance; this practice goes back to remote times. In the era of Flourishing Zhou, the prayers recorded by the scribe in the Metal-Bound Coffer (Jinteng) were kept so secret that even the Duke of Bi and the Duke of Shao were not privy to them. Yet in later ages there were those who presented their records to the throne every month, and those who wished to speak openly of the ruler's conduct at court…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
後付史館者是遵何道哉漢有禁中起
居注有太史令唐有起居郎舍人制宜
善矣迺建武貞觀開元間其故可考而
鏡也果於君治能裨益否歟宋則有時
政記有起居注有日曆有實錄又有邇
英延義記注法綦詳矣然當時諸臣有
言史官欲書而不得書與不敢書者安
在有言記注之失有四又有欲設四類
以求之者可得聞歟
===
皇上申明
祖制復脩史職蓋曠典也今
御朝有書
講筵有書
禁中起居得與聞乎諸司供報其情狀始末
可得覈其實歟夫
宮禁嚴邃聽睹靡真紀載瀚繁蒐訪難悉或
者尚議及焉抑果然歟茲欲據事直書
信今傳後必何術而可諸生樂觀盛典
punctuated: 後付史館者，是遵何道哉？漢有《禁中起居注》，有太史令；唐有起居郎、舍人，制宜善矣。迺建武、貞觀、開元間，其故可考而鏡也，果於君治能裨益否歟？宋則有《時政記》，有《起居注》，有《日曆》，有《實錄》，又有邇英、延義《記注》，法綦詳矣。然當時諸臣有言史官欲書而不得書，與不敢書者，安在？有言記注之失有四，又有欲設四類以求之者，可得聞歟？皇上申明祖制，復脩史職，蓋曠典也。今御朝有書，講筵有書，禁中起居得與聞乎？諸司供報，其情狀始末可得覈其實歟？夫宮禁嚴邃，聽睹靡真；紀載瀚繁，蒐訪難悉。或者尚議及焉，抑果然歟？茲欲據事直書，信今傳後，必何術而可？諸生樂觀盛典，
translation_en:
… and subsequently hand them over to the Historiography Institute—what principle did they follow in doing so? The Han dynasty had the Imperial Diary Within the Palace Precincts (Jinzhong qijuzhu) and the Grand Astrologer (Taishi ling); the Tang dynasty had the Court Diarists (Qiju lang) and Imperial Diarists (Qiju sheren)—their institutions ought to have been sound. Yet during the Jianwu [25–56 CE], Zhenguan [627–649], and Kaiyuan [713–741] eras, the historical precedents can be examined and held up as a mirror: were they truly able to benefit and assist the ruler's governance or not? In the Song dynasty, there were the Records of Current Administration (Shizheng ji), the Imperial Diaries (Qijuzhu), the Daily Calendars (Rili), and the Veritable Records (Shilu), as well as the Diaries of Activity and Repose for the Erying and Yanyi Pavilions; the regulations were extremely detailed. Yet among the officials of that time, some said there were matters that the historiographers wished to record but could not, or did not dare to record—what were they? Others said there were four failings in the recording of the diaries, and still others wished to establish four categories by which to seek out materials—can we hear about these?

His Majesty has reaffirmed the ancestral system and restored the duties of the historiographers, which is indeed an extraordinary grace rarely seen. Today, audiences at court are recorded, and the Classics Colloquia (Jiangyan) are recorded; yet can the daily activities within the palace precincts become known to the historiographers? As for the reports submitted by the various offices, can the full circumstances and details be verified for their truth? Now, the palace precincts are strictly guarded and secluded, so what is heard and seen may not be authentic; the records are vast and numerous, so gathering and investigating them is difficult to do exhaustively. Some still raise discussions about this—is it really so? If we now wish to write directly on the basis of the facts, so as to be trusted in the present and transmitted to posterity, by what method can this be achieved? You students have rejoiced in witnessing this grand institution…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
久矣儻有裨史職萬一者幸悉意陳之
執事者甚願與聞也
問學古有獲自昔記之矣士未有識達治
理而不藉于學者迺古人所爲學犖然
獨著于世何歟伊尹誦讀于畎畆矣異
日者卽以其君民而堯舜之太公磻谿
釣叟耳後車一載起爲王者師豈功業
固自有本抑誦讀外別有學歟後之士
或有不盡然者焉姑舉數子評之詔對
賢良者見斥于轅生號通經書者失身
于王氏自負稽古之力而誇榮車馬能
震關西之名而溺情聲伎羣書博極矣
何爲著美新之文經術經世矣何爲釀
新法之變之數子者非當時所稱宏覽
博學士乎事功類鄙屑若此矣君子有
遺譏焉豈學固不足以致用抑所以爲
學者尚未實歟
明興敦崇實學百餘年間士大夫罔不雅志
punctuated:
久矣，儻有裨史職萬一者，幸悉意陳之，執事者甚願與聞也。
問：「學古有獲」，自昔記之矣。士未有識達治理而不藉于學者。迺古人所爲學，犖然獨著于世，何歟？伊尹誦讀于畎畆矣，異日者卽以其君民而堯舜之；太公磻谿釣叟耳，後車一載，起爲王者師。豈功業固自有本，抑誦讀外別有學歟？後之士或有不盡然者焉，姑舉數子評之：詔對賢良者，見斥于轅生；號通經書者，失身于王氏；自負稽古之力，而誇榮車馬；能震關西之名，而溺情聲伎；羣書博極矣，何爲著《美新》之文？經術經世矣，何爲釀新法之變？之數子者，非當時所稱宏覽博學士乎？事功類鄙屑若此矣，君子有遺譏焉。豈學固不足以致用，抑所以爲學者尚未實歟？明興，敦崇實學，百餘年間，士大夫罔不雅志
translation_en:
… for a long time. If you have anything that might benefit the Office of Historiography even in the slightest, please set forth your thoughts in full; those in charge of this examination very much wish to hear them.

Question: "In studying antiquity one achieves gains"—this has been recorded since days of old. There has never been a scholar who understood the principles of governance without relying on learning. Yet why is it that the learning of the ancients stood out so brilliantly in the world? Yi Yin (伊尹) chanted and read in the furrowed fields, and on a later day he straightway made his ruler and people like Yao and Shun. Taigong (太公) was merely an old fisherman of the Pan Stream (磻谿), yet once carried back in the rear carriage, he rose to become the teacher of a true king. Is it that meritorious achievement inherently has its own foundation, or is there another kind of learning outside of chanting and reading texts? Among the scholars of later times, there were some who were not entirely like this. Let us tentatively cite several figures to evaluate them: he who responded to the imperial decree examining the Worthy and Excellent (賢良) [Gongsun Hong 公孫弘] was rebuked by Master Yuan [Yuan Gu 轅固]; he who was acclaimed as thoroughly versed in the classics and writings [Liu Xin 劉歆 /孔光] compromised his integrity with the Wang clan [Wang Mang 王莽]; he who prided himself on the power of his study of antiquity [Huan Rong 桓榮] boasted of the glory of his carriages and horses; he who could make his reputation resound West of the Pass (關西) [Ma Rong 馬融] indulged his passions in music and female entertainers; he who had exhaustively mastered all books [Yang Xiong 揚雄]—why did he compose the essay "Praising the Xin" (美新)? He who ordered the world through classical scholarship [Wang Anshi 王安石]—why did he brew the upheaval of the New Policies (新法)? Were these several men not what their contemporaries called scholars of vast reading and broad learning? Yet their deeds and achievements were mostly base and trivial like this, and gentlemen have left behind criticisms of them. Is it that learning is inherently insufficient for practical application, or is it that the way they pursued learning was not yet substantive?

When the Ming arose, it esteemed and promoted substantive learning (實學). For over a hundred years, scholar-officials without exception held refined ambitions …

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
好修翊戴
景運彬彬盛焉迨後操觚者溺浮詞議政者
鮮實蹟論者猶或惜之抑流弊則有然
歟夫今之士養之學校而用之科目者
其法稱善矣迺流弊若此豈成法固在
而行者寖失其意遂致是歟玆欲抑浮
詞而臻實蹟庶幾哉古所謂學必何術
而可蓋有司所以來爲求士也士則不
振拔于學竊愧之其酌所聞以復我
===
問古今譚濟理者衆矣大凡不出飭吏治
云夫吏治在辨於名實其有以先實後
名或循名責實爲言者於治體亦有識
焉否歟自昔明聖之朝治效鮮儷此載
往籍可睹也豈諸臣勵翼之實固有賴
歟叔世而下初治稍足嘉尚後迺益陵
夷也或謂漢猶近古唐次之宋逾不逮
當時且有議焉其故何歟
明興以來熙平餘二百年試觀
punctuated:
好修，翊戴景運，彬彬盛焉。迨後操觚者溺浮詞，議政者鮮實蹟，論者猶或惜之，抑流弊則有然歟？夫今之士，養之學校而用之科目者，其法稱善矣。迺流弊若此，豈成法固在，而行者寖失其意，遂致是歟？玆欲抑浮詞而臻實蹟，庶幾哉古所謂學，必何術而可？蓋有司所以來爲求士也，士則不振拔于學，竊愧之。其酌所聞以復我。

問：古今譚濟理者衆矣，大凡不出飭吏治云。夫吏治在辨於名實，其有以先實後名、或循名責實爲言者，於治體亦有識焉否歟？自昔明聖之朝，治效鮮儷，此載往籍可睹也，豈諸臣勵翼之實固有賴歟？叔世而下，初治稍足嘉尚，後迺益陵夷也。或謂漢猶近古，唐次之，宋逾不逮，當時且有議焉，其故何歟？明興以來，熙平餘二百年，試觀
translation_en:
… fond of self-cultivation, assisting and supporting the glorious destiny of the dynasty in a refined and flourishing manner. Later on, however, writers of essays indulged in华丽 empty verbiage, and those who deliberated on governance rarely achieved concrete accomplishments. Commentators have sometimes lamented this—or is it simply the natural result of accumulated abuses over time? Now, the system of nurturing today's scholars in schools and selecting them for office through the examination categories is rightly praised as excellent. Yet the abuses have come to this: is it that although the established regulations remain intact, those who administer them have gradually lost sight of their original intent, thereby bringing this about? If we now wish to curb empty verbiage and achieve concrete accomplishments, so as to approximate what the ancients called true learning, by what method can this be done? Indeed, the authorities have come here to seek out capable scholars; if scholars fail to rouse and distinguish themselves in learning, I privately feel ashamed of it. Weigh what you have learned and reply to me.

Question: Throughout antiquity and the present, many have discoursed on the art of governance and ordering the realm, and in general their views go no further than rectifying the administration of officials. Now, the administration of officials lies in distinguishing between name and reality. As for those who have advocated putting reality first and reputation second, or demanding that reality correspond to title, did they truly understand the essential principles of governance or not? Since antiquity, during the reigns of enlightened and sage rulers, the efficacy of their governance has rarely been matched; this is recorded in historical texts and can be clearly seen. Was this not indeed dependent upon the genuine efforts of their various ministers in assisting and supporting them? From the eras of decline onward, governance at the founding of a dynasty was somewhat worthy of praise, yet later it increasingly deteriorated. Some say that the Han dynasty was still close to antiquity, the Tang came next, while the Song fell even further short, attracting criticism even in its own time—what is the reason for this? Since the rise of the Ming, peace and prosperity have endured for over two hundred years. If we examine …

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
國初時政教脩明涖官者惟守法奉公以玷
清議是懼故吏治赫然稱盛其後良法
美意固在也較曩昔若少衰焉識者竊
謂沿襲久而玩愒生則然矣抑有可指
言者歟今
天子踐阼痛懲時弊
明詔屢下崇實黜虛蓋可謂惓切矣諸司固
多感激砥修以圖稱塞者而尚未盡復
諸舊豈奉行
===
德意者未至抑士習不易遽變歟夫吏治振
飭誠在士大夫之責今士習何若迺亦
可言其槩歟茲欲挽回故習名與實稱
庶幾治古必有說焉諸士其究言之此
當事者所急欲聞也
問所謂俊傑者豈非以識時務哉顧時有
緩急務有先後非可以嘗試而臆說者
以今所宜務何先也或謂北虜款矣而
互市之欲難厭南兵練矣而驕養之習
punctuated:
國初時，政教脩明，涖官者惟守法奉公，以玷清議是懼，故吏治赫然稱盛。其後良法美意固在也，較曩昔若少衰焉。識者竊謂沿襲久而玩愒生，則然矣，抑有可指言者歟？今天子踐阼，痛懲時弊，明詔屢下，崇實黜虛，蓋可謂惓切矣。諸司固多感激砥修，以圖稱塞者，而尚未盡復諸舊，豈奉行德意者未至，抑士習不易遽變歟？夫吏治振飭，誠在士大夫之責。今士習何若？迺亦可言其槩歟？茲欲挽回故習，名與實稱，庶幾治古，必有說焉。諸士其究言之，此當事者所急欲聞也。

問：所謂俊傑者，豈非以識時務哉？顧時有緩急，務有先後，非可以嘗試而臆說者。以今所宜務，何先也？或謂北虜款矣，而互市之欲難厭；南兵練矣，而驕養之習
translation_en:
… At the founding of the dynasty, governance and instruction were well-ordered and clear. Those who held office solely abided by the law and devoted themselves to the public good, fearing only that they might sully pure public opinion; thus, administrative governance was illustriously praised as flourishing. Thereafter, although the good laws and fine intentions certainly remained, compared with former times they seemed slightly declined. Discerning observers privately remark that when customs are followed for a long time, negligence and idleness arise—this is indeed so, yet are there specific points that can be identified and spoken of? Now the Son of Heaven has ascended the throne and sharply admonishes the abuses of the age. Illustrious edicts have been repeatedly handed down to exalt substance and dismiss falsehood, which may indeed be called earnest and urgent. Among the various offices, there are certainly many who, moved to gratitude, hone and cultivate themselves in hopes of fulfilling their duties, yet they have not completely restored the old standards. Is it that those who carry out His virtuous intentions have fallen short, or is it that the habits of the literati cannot easily be changed all at once? Now, the invigoration and rectification of administrative governance is truly the responsibility of the scholar-officials. What are the habits of the literati like today? Can their general outlines also be stated? If we now wish to reverse entrenched habits so that name and reality correspond, coming close to the well-governed antiquity, there must be an explanation for how to do so. Let you gentlemen speak of this exhaustively, for this is what those in authority are eager to hear.

Question: Is not he who is called an outstanding man of talent so named because he understands the affairs of the times? Yet times have their urgencies and relaxations, and affairs have their priorities and sequences; they are not things that can be approached by trial and error or subjective conjecture. Among the affairs that ought to be attended to today, what comes first? Some say that the northern caitiffs have submitted to tribute terms, yet their desires in border trade are hard to satiate; the southern troops have been trained, yet their habits of arrogant coddling…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
難馴河渠歲決而漕糧患不通鹽法日
壞而邊儲患不實數者皆
國家重務計無先於此者然歟否歟抑所謂
關天下之安危而爲社稷至計者猶有
出於此歟或又謂天下安否在紀綱風
俗紀綱誠振風俗誠正卽他無足慮者
其信然歟今日之紀綱風俗果何如歟
何道可以振而正之也諸士憂先天下
志焉
punctuated: 難馴；河渠歲決，而漕糧患不通；鹽法日壞，而邊儲患不實。數者皆國家重務，計無先於此者，然歟否歟？抑所謂關天下之安危，而爲社稷至計者，猶有出於此歟？或又謂天下安否在紀綱風俗，紀綱誠振，風俗誠正，卽他無足慮者，其信然歟？今日之紀綱風俗果何如歟？何道可以振而正之也？諸士憂先天下，志焉。
translation_en: … is hard to tame; the rivers and canals breach every year, and the grain tribute suffers from blockages; the salt administration deteriorates day by day, and frontier provisions suffer from depletion. All several of these are weighty affairs of the Dynasty, and no policy takes precedence over them—is this so or not? Or is there still something beyond these that pertains to the security and peril of the empire and constitutes the supreme plan for the altars of soil and grain? Others again say that the security or peril of the empire lies in discipline and customs—that if discipline is truly invigorated and customs are truly rectified, then nothing else is worth worrying about. Is this truly so? What is the actual state of discipline and customs today? By what way can they be invigorated and rectified? You scholars, who worry before the rest of the world worries, direct your thoughts [?] to this.

四書
子曰道千乘之國敬事而信節用而愛人
使民以時
史繼辰

〔允足爲崇雅之範〕

〔佳士佳士〕
===

〔録之以式多士〕

聖人揭治國之要皆心乎民而已葢民者國之
本也治國而一以民爲心焉茲其所以爲有要
歟夫子示萬世治道之凖也葢謂千乘之國大
國也道之者將使各得其理也是豈可把持於
法制之末乎又豈可粉飾於文爲之具乎葢有
punctuated:
第壹場：四書。

「子曰：『道千乘之國，敬事而信，節用而愛人，使民以時。』」

史繼辰

同考試官教諭王　批：〔清楚矯健，迥出凡流，允足爲崇雅之範。〕
同考試官教諭伍　批：〔體裁純雅，詞旨舂容，佳士，佳士。〕
同考試官教諭李　批：〔削蔓剔浮，獨標理㒒，録之以式多士。〕

考試官左中允戴　批：〔簡當得體。〕

聖人揭治國之要，皆心乎民而已。葢民者，國之本也。治國而一以民爲心焉，茲其所以爲有要歟？夫子示萬世治道之凖也。葢謂千乘之國，大國也；道之者，將使各得其理也。是豈可把持於法制之末乎？又豈可粉飾於文爲之具乎？葢有
translation_en:
First Session: Four Books

"The Master said: 'In guiding a state of a thousand war-chariots, be reverent toward public affairs and trustworthy, be frugal in expenditure and love the people, and employ the common folk only in the proper seasons.'" (Analects 1.5)

Shi Jichen 史繼辰

Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang comments: [Clear and vigorous, standing far above the ordinary run of essays; truly worthy to serve as a model for exalting elegance.]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: [Pure and refined in structure, calm and unhurried in diction and purport—an excellent scholar, an excellent scholar!]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li comments: [Pruning away rambling overgrowth and stripping off superficiality, it alone sets forth unadorned principle; record it as a model for the many scholars.]
Examiner and Right Admonisher (you zanshan) Chen comments: [Without wasting words, its meaning is complete; it ought to be recorded as a model.]
Examiner and Left Companion (zuo zhongyun) Dai comments: [Concise, apt, and fitting in style.]

When the Sage sets forth the essentials of governing a state, all of them center in his heart upon the common people, and nothing more. For the people are the root of the state. In governing a state, to keep one's heart wholly upon the people—is this not why governance possesses its essentials? The Master was thereby showing the standard for the way of governance for ten thousand generations. What he meant is that a state of a thousand war-chariots is a great state, and to guide it is to cause everything within it to attain its proper order. How could this be achieved merely by clinging to the superficialities of laws and regulations? And how could it be achieved by glossing things over with the trappings of outward ceremony and artifice? Indeed, there are…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
要焉不能無事而一不敬或貽害於民矣必兢
業爲防而細微之動亦若有所於警戒者況大
事乎且一念之誠確謹於前而不改於後而常如
金石之堅固也紛更以滋擾者又其所不爲也
已不能無用而一不節或多取於民矣必量入
爲出而經常之費亦若有所於限制者況冗費
乎且一念之惻怛愛其人惟恐其傷而常如天
地之好生也苛刻而寡恩者又其所不忍也已
至若國有興作不能不使乎民而非其時則民
===
務妨矣又必於農隙之際而後敢以動大衆起
大役焉可曰國事之當急也而遂以民事爲可
緩乎夫敬信也節愛也使以時也心無一而不
爲乎民則事也用也人民也國無一而不得其
理於千乘之治乎何有大抵治本於道道本於
心心乎爲民則雖文法未備而上無失道民有
受其惠者心乎爲巳則法度文章之施將或違
道以干譽而實意彌衰實惠彌寡矣是故敬者
所以持其心而適於道者也此夫子所以首言
punctuated: 要焉。不能無事，而一不敬，或貽害於民矣。必兢業爲防，而細微之動，亦若有所於警戒者，況大事乎？且一念之誠確，謹於前而不改於後，而常如金石之堅固也，紛更以滋擾者，又其所不爲也已。不能無用，而一不節，或多取於民矣。必量入爲出，而經常之費，亦若有所於限制者，況冗費乎？且一念之惻怛，愛其人惟恐其傷，而常如天地之好生也，苛刻而寡恩者，又其所不忍也已。至若國有興作，不能不使乎民，而非其時，則民務妨矣。又必於農隙之際，而後敢以動大衆、起大役，焉可曰國事之當急也，而遂以民事爲可緩乎？夫敬信也、節愛也、使以時也，心無一而不爲乎民；則事也、用也、人民也，國無一而不得其理，於千乘之治乎何有？大抵治本於道，道本於心。心乎爲民，則雖文法未備，而上無失道，民有受其惠者；心乎爲巳，則法度文章之施，將或違道以干譽，而實意彌衰，實惠彌寡矣。是故敬者，所以持其心而適於道者也，此夫子所以首言
translation_en: …essentials to it. One cannot be without state affairs, yet a single lapse in reverence toward them may bring harm to the people. One must guard against this with cautious diligence, so that even in minor undertakings there seems to be a sense of vigilance—how much more so in great affairs! Moreover, with a single-minded sincerity and firmness, being careful at the outset and unchanging afterward, always as steadfast as metal and stone, one will certainly never engage in erratic changes that only breed disturbance. One cannot be without expenditures, yet a single lapse in frugality may lead to excessive extraction from the people. One must regulate outlays according to income, so that even regular expenses seem to be subject to strict limits—how much more so superfluous expenditures! Moreover, with a single-minded compassion, loving the people and only fearing they might be harmed, always like Heaven and Earth in their love of life, one can certainly never bear to be harsh and ungenerous. As for when the state has construction projects, one cannot avoid employing the people; yet if it is not done at the proper season, the people's agricultural tasks will be hindered. Thus one must wait until the intervals between farming seasons before daring to mobilize the multitude and initiate major corvée labor. How could one say that state affairs are urgent and consequently treat the people's livelihood as something that can be delayed? Now, in being reverent and trustworthy, in being frugal and loving, and in employing the people according to the proper season, there is not a single thought in the ruler's mind that is not for the sake of the people. Consequently, in affairs, in expenditures, and in the populace, there is nothing in the state that does not attain its proper order—what difficulty, then, could there be in governing a state of a thousand chariots? In general, governance is rooted in the Way, and the Way is rooted in the mind. When the mind is devoted to the people, even if legal statutes and regulations are not yet complete, the ruler above does not stray from the Way, and the people below receive his benefits. When the mind is devoted to oneself, the implementation of laws, institutions, and outward forms will perhaps violate the Way in order to seek praise, while genuine intent increasingly declines and actual benefits grow ever scarcer. Therefore, reverence is that by which one holds fast to one's mind and conforms to the Way; this is why the Master spoke of it first…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之也
誠者自成也而道自道也誠者物之終始
不誠無物是故君子誠之爲貴誠者非
自成已而已也所以成物也成已仁也
成物知也性之德也合外內之道也故
時措之宜也
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔詞意圓融格調莊整〕
顧憲成
〔而脉絡過接處渾無痕迹中庸義之最佳者可〕
錄以式
===
同考試官教授黄　批〔見理精審措詞簡當〕
〔以誠自成句揔括一章大旨自道所以自成意〕
〔躍然言表非淺學可到〕
考試官右賛善陳　批〔說理之文自是精切〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔圓融周足〕
中庸原誠切于人而君子能體其全也夫誠成
天下之性而時措之則道也君子存誠而成已
成物之道統是矣且人之一心萬物咸備者焉
punctuated:
之也。

「誠者，自成也；而道，自道也。誠者，物之終始，不誠無物。是故君子誠之爲貴。誠者，非自成已而已也，所以成物也。成已，仁也；成物，知也。性之德也，合外內之道也，故時措之宜也。」

顧憲成
同考試官教諭蔣　批：〔詞意圓融，格調莊整，〕〔而脉絡過接處渾無痕迹，《中庸》義之最佳者，可〕錄以式。
同考試官教授黄　批：〔見理精審，措詞簡當。〕〔以「誠自成」句揔括一章大旨，「自道所以自成」意〕〔躍然言表，非淺學可到。〕
考試官右賛善陳　批：〔說理之文，自是精切。〕
考試官左中允戴　批：〔圓融周足。〕

《中庸》原誠切于人，而君子能體其全也。夫誠成天下之性，而時措之則道也；君子存誠，而成已成物之道統是矣。且人之一心，萬物咸備者焉。
translation_en:
… it first.

"Sincerity is that whereby self-completion is effected, and its Way is that by which one must direct oneself. Sincerity is the end and beginning of things; without sincerity there would be nothing. Therefore the superior man regards the attainment of sincerity as the most noble pursuit. The possessor of sincerity does not merely accomplish the self-completion of himself; with this quality he also completes other things and men. The completion of himself shows his perfect virtue (ren); the completion of other things shows his wisdom (zhi). Both are virtues belonging to human nature, and this is the Way by which a union of the external and internal is effected. Therefore, whenever he employs them, his actions are fitting to the time."

Gu Xiancheng 顧憲成
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Jiang comments: [The wording and meaning are harmonious and well-rounded, the style is solemn and orderly, and the transitions along the logical thread are completely seamless. It is the finest among the essays on the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), worthy of] being recorded as a model.
Associate Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Huang comments: [Its grasp of principle is precise and thorough, and its phrasing is concise and apt. Using the clause "sincerity is that whereby self-completion is effected" to encompass the main purport of the entire chapter, the idea that "one directs oneself in order to achieve self-completion" leaps vividly from beyond the words—something no shallow scholar could attain.]
Examiner and Right Admonisher Chen comments: [As an essay expounding moral principle, it is naturally precise and incisive.]
Examiner and Left Companion to the Heir Apparent Dai comments: [Harmonious, well-rounded, and thoroughly complete.]

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) traces how sincerity is intimately tied to humanity, and how the superior man is able to embody it in its entirety. Now, sincerity brings to completion the nature of all under Heaven, and when applied fittingly according to the time, it is the Way; when the superior man preserves sincerity, the Way of completing both the self and all things is unified therein. Moreover, within the single mind of man, all the myriad things are completely contained. …

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
自物理具于心而眞實無妄者謂之誠誠卽道
之體而物所自成也自物理見于行而時措咸
宜者謂之道道卽誠之用而人當自道也何言
乎蓋一始一終者物之成而始之終之者誠之
爲苟無是誠則無是物矣是故君子知物非誠
不立必存誠以求物與之原以誠非道不行當
體道以爲誠身之實斯固以自成耳然誠而自
成非虛也卽成其與物爲體者也誠之而自道
非已也卽道其所以成物者也蓋成已爲仁成
===
物爲知德同出于所性而仁非有內知非有外
道實合于一原故一誠立而性盡矣性盡而仁
智之道備矣以之成已者卽以之成物而神應
不窮由此裕內者亦由此利外而時出不匱是
措之爲道信乎自道也而孰非以自成哉此君
子必以誠爲貴也嗟夫誠無人已道無內外君
子盡人盡物而參賛化育皆以自成非爲物也
聖賢每對擧以言豈誠有先後次第哉蓋卽已
卽物而成物者正所以成已耳無對待亦無先
punctuated: 自物理具于心，而眞實無妄者謂之誠，誠卽道之體，而物所自成也；自物理見于行，而時措咸宜者謂之道，道卽誠之用，而人當自道也。何言乎？蓋一始一終者物之成，而始之終之者誠之爲，苟無是誠，則無是物矣。是故君子知物非誠不立，必存誠以求物與之原；以誠非道不行，當體道以爲誠身之實。斯固以自成耳。然誠而自成，非虛也，卽成其與物爲體者也；誠之而自道，非已也，卽道其所以成物者也。蓋成已爲仁，成物爲知，德同出于所性；而仁非有內，知非有外，道實合于一原。故一誠立而性盡矣，性盡而仁智之道備矣。以之成已者卽以之成物，而神應不窮；由此裕內者亦由此利外，而時出不匱。是措之爲道，信乎自道也，而孰非以自成哉！此君子必以誠爲貴也。嗟夫！誠無人已，道無內外。君子盡人盡物而參賛化育，皆以自成，非爲物也。聖賢每對擧以言，豈誠有先後次第哉？蓋卽已卽物，而成物者正所以成已耳，無對待亦無先
translation_en: … As the principles of things are inherent in the mind, that which is real and free from falsity is called sincerity (cheng); sincerity is the substance of the Way (dao) and that whereby things complete themselves. As the principles of things are manifested in action, that which is entirely fitting when timely applied is called the Way; the Way is the function of sincerity and that which man ought to pursue for himself. Why do we say this? For having a beginning and an end is the completion of a thing, while initiating it and bringing it to an end is the work of sincerity; if there were not this sincerity, there would be no such thing. Therefore, the superior man knows that without sincerity things cannot be established, so he must preserve sincerity in order to seek the source with which things are endowed; and knowing that without the Way sincerity cannot be put into practice, he must embody the Way as the reality of making his own person sincere. This is indeed how he completes himself. Yet being sincere and completing oneself is not something empty: it is completing that which forms one body with all things. Attaining sincerity and pursuing the Way for oneself is not merely for oneself: it is pursuing that whereby things are completed. For completing oneself is humanity (ren), and completing things is wisdom (zhi)—both virtues issue alike from our endowed nature; and since humanity is not exclusively internal nor wisdom exclusively external, their Ways truly unite in a single source. Thus, once sincerity is established, one's nature is fully realized; and once one's nature is fully realized, the Way of humanity and wisdom is complete. That by which one completes oneself is the very means by which one completes things, responding miraculously without exhaustion; that from which one enriches the interior is also that from which one benefits the exterior, issuing forth at the proper time without fail. Thus, applying it in practice as the Way is truly pursuing the Way for oneself, and what part of it is not a means of completing oneself? This is why the superior man must prize sincerity. Alas! Sincerity knows no distinction between others and self, and the Way knows no division between inner and outer. When the superior man fully realizes the nature of other men and of things, and assists in the transforming and nourishing processes of Heaven and Earth, all of it is to complete himself, not for the sake of external things. Sages and worthies often speak of them as paired counterparts, but does sincerity really have a sequence of before and after? Rather, self and things are identical, and completing things is precisely the means of completing oneself; there is neither opposition nor priority…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
後故揔謂曰誠者自成此子思善于立言歟
舉舜而敷治焉舜使益掌火益烈山澤而
焚之禽獸逃匿禹疏九河瀹濟漯而注
諸海決汝漢排淮泗而注之江然後中
國可得而食也當是時也禹八年於外
三過其門而不入雖欲耕得乎后稷教
民稼穡樹藝五穀五穀熟而民人育人
之有道也飽食煖衣逸居而無教則近
於禽獸聖人有憂之使契爲司徒教以
人倫父子有親君臣有義夫婦有別長
幼有序朋友有信放勳曰勞之來之匡
之直之輔之翼之使自得之又從而振
德之聖人之憂民如此而暇耕乎堯以
不得舜爲已憂舜以不得禹皐陶爲已
憂夫以百畝之不易爲已憂者農夫也
陳所蘊
同考試官教諭林　批〔體格峻整詞華高雅〕
不惟工於長題而且灼見堯舜用心者佳士也
punctuated:
後，故揔謂曰：「誠者自成。」此子思善于立言歟！

「舉舜而敷治焉。舜使益掌火，益烈山澤而焚之，禽獸逃匿。禹疏九河，瀹濟、漯而注諸海，決汝、漢，排淮、泗而注之江，然後中國可得而食也。當是時也，禹八年於外，三過其門而不入，雖欲耕，得乎？后稷教民稼穡，樹藝五穀；五穀熟而民人育。人之有道也，飽食、煖衣、逸居而無教，則近於禽獸。聖人有憂之，使契爲司徒，教以人倫：父子有親，君臣有義，夫婦有別，長幼有序，朋友有信。放勳曰：『勞之來之，匡之直之，輔之翼之，使自得之，又從而振德之。』聖人之憂民如此，而暇耕乎？堯以不得舜爲已憂，舜以不得禹、皐陶爲已憂。夫以百畝之不易爲已憂者，農夫也。」
陳所蘊
同考試官教諭林　批：〔體格峻整，詞華高雅，〕不惟工於長題，而且灼見堯、舜用心者，佳士也。
translation_en:
… sequence, and therefore he summed it up overall by saying: "Sincerity is self-completion." How skilled Zisi 子思 was in establishing his words!

"He raised up Shun 舜 to spread governance everywhere. Shun appointed Yi 益 to take charge of fire; Yi set fire to the mountains and marshes and burned them, and the birds and beasts fled and hid. Yu 禹 dredged the Nine Rivers, cleared the Ji 濟 and Ta 漯 rivers and channeled them into the sea, opened up the Ru 汝 and Han 漢 rivers, and diverted the Huai 淮 and Si 泗 rivers to channel them into the Yangtze, and only after this could the Central Land obtain food to eat. At that time, Yu spent eight years away from home and three times passed the door of his own house without entering; even if he had wished to plow the fields himself, could he have done so? Hou Ji 后稷 taught the people to sow and reap, and to cultivate the five grains; when the five grains ripened, the people were nourished. The way of human beings is such that if they eat their fill, wear warm clothes, and live in comfort without instruction, they become close to birds and beasts. The Sage was worried about this, and so he appointed Xie 契 to be Minister of Education (Situ 司徒) to teach them the human relationships: that between father and son there should be affection, between ruler and minister righteousness, between husband and wife distinction, between old and young proper order, and between friends faithfulness. Fangxun 放勳 [Yao 堯] said: 'Encourage them, lead them on, rectify them, straighten them, help them, give them wings, so as to cause them to attain it for themselves, and then follow this up by stimulating them and conferring kindness upon them.' When the Sage's concern for the people was like this, did he have the leisure to plow? Yao took failure to find a Shun as his personal worry; Shun took failure to find a Yu and a Gao Yao 皐陶 as his personal worry. As for one who takes failure to properly till his hundred mu of land as his personal worry, he is merely a farmer."

By Chen Suoyun 陳所蘊.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Lin 林: 〔Its structure is lofty and well-ordered, its literary elegance elevated and refined.〕 Not only is he skilled at handling a long examination topic, he also clearly perceives the minds of Yao and Shun—a fine scholar indeed.

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭汪　批〔體裁簡當詞調高古〕
最得作長題之法者宜錄以式
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔布置有倫而且辭氣〕
馴雅長題之最優者允可以錄矣
同考試官教諭王　批〔場中作者類牽涉上〕
文殊非題意此篇就題發揮精切簡當可爲作
長題者式
考試官右賛善陳　批〔詞理簡明〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔以人已立說得旨〕
===
大賢叙聖人之任諸人者表聖人之責諸巳者
蓋巳不可以徧爲也聖人先任人而巳之責塞
矣何以耕爲哉孟子所以闢許行也意謂聖人
之憂天下無窮聖人之爲天下有要使與民竝
耕而爲賢宜莫如堯舜矣然吾觀堯之爲君也
不自爲也側陋揚而登庸之命屬於舜焉百揆
納而俾乂之司屬於舜焉蓋方任一相以爲之
總理也而他無暇也舜之爲相也亦不自爲也
以烈山使益而禹乃治水雖門之三過弗顧焉
punctuated:
同考試官教諭汪批：〔體裁簡當，詞調高古，〕最得作長題之法者，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭鄧批：〔布置有倫，而且辭氣〕馴雅，長題之最優者，允可以錄矣。
同考試官教諭王批：〔場中作者類牽涉上〕文，殊非題意。此篇就題發揮，精切簡當，可爲作長題者式。
考試官右賛善陳批：〔詞理簡明。〕
考試官左中允戴批：〔以人已立說，得旨。〕
大賢叙聖人之任諸人者，表聖人之責諸巳者。蓋巳不可以徧爲也，聖人先任人而巳之責塞矣，何以耕爲哉？孟子所以闢許行也。意謂：聖人之憂天下無窮，聖人之爲天下有要。使與民竝耕而爲賢，宜莫如堯、舜矣。然吾觀堯之爲君也，不自爲也。側陋揚而登庸之命屬於舜焉，百揆納而俾乂之司屬於舜焉。蓋方任一相以爲之總理也，而他無暇也。舜之爲相也，亦不自爲也。以烈山使益而禹乃治水，雖門之三過弗顧焉；
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 汪 comments: "[Its structural form is concise and fitting, and its diction and tone are lofty and archaic;] it has best grasped the method for composing essays on long topics, and ought to be printed as a model."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Deng 鄧 comments: "[Its arrangement is orderly, and furthermore its diction and vitality] are refined and elegant. It is the finest of essays on a long topic, and truly worthy of being printed for the record."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: "[In the examination hall, writers generally dragged in the preceding] passage of the text, which was quite contrary to the purport of the topic. This essay develops its argument strictly from the topic itself—precise, incisive, concise, and fitting—and can serve as a model for those composing on long topics."
Examiner and Right Admonisher Chen 陳 comments: "[Its diction and reasoning are concise and clear.]"
Examiner and Left Companion Dai 戴 comments: "[By framing the argument around the contrast between others and oneself, it captures the main purport.]"

The Great Worthy recounts what the Sages entrusted to others in order to bring to light what the Sages demanded of themselves. For indeed, one cannot do everything oneself; when the Sages first entrusted responsibilities to others, their own duty was fulfilled—what need was there to plough? This was how Mencius 孟子 refuted Xu Xing 許行. His meaning is as follows: The Sages' anxiety for the world is boundless, yet the Sages' governance of the world has its essentials. If ploughing alongside the people were what constituted worthiness, then surely none would have surpassed Yao 堯 and Shun 舜 in doing so. Yet when I observe how Yao acted as ruler, he did not do everything himself. Once he raised up one from humble obscurity, the mandate of elevation and employment was entrusted to Shun; once Shun was received as General Regulator, the charge of bringing order was entrusted to Shun. For he was just then employing a single chief minister to oversee the general administration for him, and had no leisure for anything else. And when Shun acted as chief minister, he too did not do everything himself. He assigned Yi 益 to burn off the vegetation on the mountains, while Yu 禹 regulated the waters, not even stopping to enter his own door though he passed it three times; …

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以樹藝使稷而契乃明倫雖民之自得未已焉
蓋方任庶官以爲之分理也而他無暇也此可
見堯之心非不憂民之憂也而不皆以責之己
也己之憂惟不得舜耳舜得而民之可憂者舜
代之矣已可無憂矣舜之心非不憂堯之憂也
而不皆以責之己也己之憂惟不得禹皐陶耳
禹皐陶得而堯之所憂者禹皐陶代之矣已可
無憂矣蓋君相之體統治道之先務有如此者
若乃受百畝之常業而憂百畝之不治此獨爲
===
農夫者則然耳彼庶官且不宜爾也而况於君
相乎哉然則許行之說之妄也果矣大抵治貴
識體事當知務務得其體則綱舉而目隨事逸
而功倍矣否則君行臣事相執有司文會愈煩
而墮惰愈甚雖堯舜且不能爲理者此孟氏所
以深憂而力辨也
易
安貞之吉應地无疆
史繼辰
punctuated:
以樹藝使稷，而契乃明倫，雖民之自得未已焉。蓋方任庶官以爲之分理也，而他無暇也。此可見堯之心非不憂民之憂也，而不皆以責之己也。己之憂，惟不得舜耳；舜得，而民之可憂者舜代之矣，已可無憂矣。舜之心非不憂堯之憂也，而不皆以責之己也。己之憂，惟不得禹、皐陶耳；禹、皐陶得，而堯之所憂者禹、皐陶代之矣，已可無憂矣。蓋君相之體統、治道之先務，有如此者。若乃受百畝之常業，而憂百畝之不治，此獨爲農夫者則然耳，彼庶官且不宜爾也，而况於君相乎哉！然則許行之說之妄也果矣。大抵治貴識體，事當知務。務得其體，則綱舉而目隨，事逸而功倍矣。否則，君行臣事，相執有司，文會愈煩而墮惰愈甚，雖堯、舜且不能爲理者，此孟氏所以深憂而力辨也。

《易》
「安貞之吉，應地无疆。」
史繼辰
translation_en:
…he employed Ji to teach the sowing and reaping of grain, and Xie then clarified human relationships, not ceasing even after the people had become self-possessed in their virtue. This is because he was just then entrusting the various officials to divide the tasks of governance among themselves, and had no leisure for anything else. From this it can be seen that the mind of Yao was not without concern for the worries of the people, yet he did not take all of those responsibilities upon himself. His only worry was failing to find Shun; once Shun was found, Shun took his place in attending to what was worrisome among the people, and he himself could be free from worry. The mind of Shun was not without concern for the worries of Yao, yet he did not take all of those responsibilities upon himself. His only worry was failing to find Yu and Gao Yao; once Yu and Gao Yao were found, Yu and Gao Yao took his place in attending to what Yao worried about, and he himself could be free from worry. Such, indeed, are the proper system of ruler and chief minister and the foremost priorities in the way of governance! As for receiving a regular allotment of a hundred mu of land and worrying that those hundred mu are not properly cultivated, this is so only for one who is a farmer. Even those various officials ought not to act thus—how much less a ruler or chief minister! Thus, the absurdity of Xu Xing's doctrine is certain indeed. On the whole, in governance one values understanding the proper system of roles, and in affairs one must know what is most urgent. When urgent tasks conform to the proper system, then once the main cord of the net is lifted, the meshes follow; the work is easy, and the achievements are doubled. Otherwise, the ruler performs the tasks of his subjects, the chief minister takes hold of the duties of the lesser functionaries, documentary accounting grows ever more burdensome while negligence and sloth grow ever worse, so that even Yao and Shun would be unable to achieve order. This is why Mencius was deeply worried and argued against it so forcefully.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"The good fortune of tranquil correctness corresponds to the boundless Earth."
Shi Jichen

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭王　批〔此題作者往往多襲故套殊爲厭觀獨此刊落浮言一敦本實佳哉〕

君子順健之善爲能配地焉夫立地之道順而
健也君子得坤道之純則何間然之有彖傳舉
===
而贊之謂夫道有造化得之成形而吾人得之
成德者順健是也吾嘗合而觀之彼坤之居後
也往西南也皆貞也而君子安焉則是循分之
所宜退讓以堅其守率素之所履久道以立其
方知天下不可先也而後之安吾居後之正而
得常之善以致矣知天下以類聚也而從之安
吾西南之正而得朋之慶以集矣是謂安貞之
吉而有不足以應地之无疆耶蓋坤厚載物地
punctuated:
同考試官教諭王批：〔此題作者往往多襲故套，殊爲厭觀。獨此刊落浮言，一敦本實，佳哉！〕
同考試官教諭伍批：〔詞簡意周，是亦法坤而有得者，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官教諭李批：〔意匪語精，非邃於《易》者不能作，錄之。〕
考試官右贊善陳批：〔詞旨簡實。〕
考試官左中允戴批：〔整潔可式。〕

君子順健之善，爲能配地焉。夫立地之道，順而健也；君子得坤道之純，則何間然之有？《彖傳》舉而贊之，謂夫道有造化得之成形，而吾人得之成德者，順健是也。吾嘗合而觀之：彼坤之居後也、往西南也，皆貞也，而君子安焉。則是循分之所宜，退讓以堅其守；率素之所履，久道以立其方。知天下不可先也而後之，安吾居後之正，而得常之善以致矣；知天下以類聚也而從之，安吾西南之正，而得朋之慶以集矣。是謂「安貞之吉」，而有不足以應地之无疆耶？蓋坤厚載物，地
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wang, comments: [Authors on this topic all too often copy old clichés, which makes for truly tedious reading. Only this essay strips away superficial verbiage and focuses entirely on fundamental substance—how excellent!]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wu, comments: [The wording is concise and the meaning comprehensive. This too comes from someone who has modeled himself on Kun and gained insight; it should be recorded as a model.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Li, comments: [The ideas are rich [?] and the language refined; none but one deeply versed in the Book of Changes (Yi) could have written this. Record it.]
Examiner, Right Admonisher Chen, comments: [The wording and import are concise and substantial.]
Examiner, Left Companion Dai, comments: [Well-ordered and clean; worthy of serving as a model.]

The goodness of the noble man's docile strength is thereby able to match the Earth. Now, the Way that establishes the Earth is docile yet strong; when the noble man attains the purity of the Way of Kun, what room is there for any discrepancy between them? The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan) singles this out for praise, meaning that there is a Way which the creative transformation receives to form physical shapes, and which we humans receive to perfect our virtue—and that is docile strength. I have considered them together: that Kun takes the rear position and goes to the southwest—both of these are firm correctness, and the noble man rests content in them. Thus he follows what is fitting for his lot, yielding modestly so as to hold fast to his resolve; he abides by his accustomed path, enduring in the Way so as to establish his squareness. Knowing that one must not put oneself ahead of the world, he stays behind it, resting content in the correctness of remaining behind, and thus attains the goodness of gaining the constant rule. Knowing that the world gathers according to kind, he follows along with it, resting content in the correctness of the southwest, and thus gathers the blessing of gaining friends. This is what is meant by "the good fortune of resting content in firm correctness"—and could it be insufficient to correspond to the boundlessness of the Earth? For Kun in its thickness supports all things, and the Earth…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之德本无疆也至柔而剛地之无疆以順健也
今惟安而貞焉是安常自守適合乎柔靜無爲
之體而其道卽坤之道强毅有執默契乎剛柔
成質之懿而其德卽坤之德地無成而代有終
也君子居後而無先倡也順以應物與順以承
天者固相肖不離矣坤居西南而致役也君子
往西南而得朋也簡而易從與簡而成能者固
合一無間矣蓋始焉法地之道以體諸身終焉
以吾之道而配諸地此君子所以與造化爲徒
===
而協大中之矩者也欲合德于坤者夫亦求端
於易簡而已大抵天地之道陰陽盡之矣人心
之德亦陰陽盡之矣陰陽卽順健也地道人道
相爲流通者也是故順健之理得而參天地贊
化育坤維且賴之以貞故曰苟非其人道不虛
行
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深也
故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成天下
之務唯神也故不疾而速不行而至子
punctuated:
之德本无疆也；至柔而剛，地之无疆以順健也。今惟安而貞焉，是安常自守，適合乎柔靜無爲之體，而其道卽坤之道；强毅有執，默契乎剛柔成質之懿，而其德卽坤之德。地無成而代有終也，君子居後而無先倡也，順以應物與順以承天者，固相肖不離矣；坤居西南而致役也，君子往西南而得朋也，簡而易從與簡而成能者，固合一無間矣。蓋始焉法地之道以體諸身，終焉以吾之道而配諸地，此君子所以與造化爲徒，而協大中之矩者也。欲合德于坤者，夫亦求端於易簡而已。大抵天地之道，陰陽盡之矣；人心之德，亦陰陽盡之矣。陰陽卽順健也，地道、人道相爲流通者也。是故順健之理得，而參天地、贊化育，坤維且賴之以貞。故曰：「苟非其人，道不虛行。」
夫《易》，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。子
translation_en:
… virtue is inherently boundless; supremely yielding yet firm, the boundlessness of Earth lies in its docile strength. Now, if one is only content and upright, then one abides in constancy and maintains self-restraint, conforming precisely to the substance of yielding tranquility and non-action—so that one's Way is none other than the Way of Kun; resolute and steadfast, one tacitly accords with the excellence of firmness and gentleness brought to completion in substance—so that one's virtue is none other than the virtue of Kun. Earth claims no achievement of its own, yet brings things to completion on behalf of Heaven; the noble man stays behind and does not take the lead: thus, responding to things with docility and receiving Heaven with docility truly resemble each other without separation. Kun dwells in the southwest and exerts its service; the noble man goes to the southwest and finds companions: thus, being simple and easy to follow and being simple and achieving capability truly unite as one without a gap. In the beginning, one models oneself upon the Way of Earth so as to embody it in one's person; in the end, one takes one's own Way and matches it with Earth. This is how the noble man becomes a companion of the creative transformation of nature and harmonizes with the standard of the Great Mean. Those who wish to unite their virtue with Kun should simply seek the beginning in ease and simplicity.

In general, the Way of Heaven and Earth is exhausted by yin and yang; the virtue of the human mind is likewise exhausted by yin and yang. Yin and yang are none other than docility and strength; the Way of Earth and the Way of Man flow into and communicate with each other. Therefore, when the principle of docility and strength is grasped, one forms a triad with Heaven and Earth and assists in the transforming and nourishing processes, and the very pillars of Earth rely upon this to remain firm. Thus it is said: "If there be not the proper person, the Way does not operate in vain."

"Now the Changes (Yi) is that by which the sages fathom the utmost depths and investigate the subtle springs of things. Because it is deep, it can penetrate the wills of all under Heaven; because it is subtle, it can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; because it is spirit-like, it makes haste without hurrying and reaches its destination without traveling. The Master…"

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
曰易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
丁奇逢
同考試官教諭王　批〔擺脫時套會文切理〕
〔深於易者也可式可式〕
同考試官教諭伍　批〔浄洗支蔓一歸雅正〕
〔杰構也錄之〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔脫去塵套獨存風骨〕
〔可爲浮靡者式〕
考試官右賛善陳　批〔語意精到〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔詞簡而意足〕
===
即易用之所以神而知其道歸諸聖矣蓋易非
聖人不能作也然所以神用於天下者具是焉
其斯爲聖道與且夫辭占象變固易道之至神
矣今乃以歸諸聖者謂何蓋來物之理隱於未
形何深也自聖人有辭占而深者從茲顯矣易
非聖人之所以極深乎動靜之端涵於莫測何
幾也自聖人有象變而幾者從茲著矣易非聖
人之所以研幾乎夫深極於辭占則辭占即深
punctuated:
曰：「《易》有聖人之道四焉者，此之謂也。」
丁奇逢
同考試官教諭王批：〔擺脫時套，會文切理，〕〔深於《易》者也，可式可式。〕
同考試官教諭伍批：〔浄洗支蔓，一歸雅正，〕〔杰構也，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭李批：〔脫去塵套，獨存風骨，〕〔可爲浮靡者式。〕
考試官右賛善陳批：〔語意精到。〕
考試官左中允戴批：〔詞簡而意足。〕
即《易》用之所以神，而知其道歸諸聖矣。蓋《易》非聖人不能作也，然所以神用於天下者具是焉，其斯爲聖道與！且夫辭、占、象、變，固《易》道之至神矣，今乃以歸諸聖者，謂何？蓋來物之理，隱於未形，何深也！自聖人有辭、占，而深者從茲顯矣，《易》非聖人之所以極深乎？動靜之端，涵於莫測，何幾也！自聖人有象、變，而幾者從茲著矣，《易》非聖人之所以研幾乎？夫深極於辭、占，則辭、占即深…
translation_en:
…said, "When it is said that the Changes (Yi) contains the fourfold Way of the Sages, this is what is meant."

Ding Qifeng 丁奇逢

Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: [Breaking free from contemporary clichés, it integrates the text and hits upon the principle;] [he is one who is profound in the Changes—a true model, a true model!]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wu 伍 comments: [Thoroughly cleansing away rambling digressions, it returns entirely to elegance and correctness.] [A masterpiece; record it for publication.]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li 李 comments: [Shedding worldly conventions, it preserves a singular strength of character;] [it can serve as a model for those given to superficiality and floridness.]
Examiner and Right Admonisher Chen 陳 comments: [The wording and meaning are precise and penetrating.]
Examiner and Left Companion Dai 戴 comments: [The diction is concise, yet the meaning is completos and full.]

By looking at how the function of the Changes operates with such spirit-like efficacy, one knows that its Way is attributable to the Sages. Indeed, none but the Sages could have created the Changes; yet that by which its spirit-like efficacy functions throughout the world is fully contained therein—is this not what makes it the Way of the Sages?

Moreover, the explanations (ci), prognostications (zhan), images (xiang), and transformations (bian) are assuredly the ultimate spirit-like efficacy of the Way of the Changes; why, then, are they now attributed to the Sages? It is because the principles of things to come lie hidden before they take form—how profound they are! Once the Sages established the explanations and prognostications, what was profound was thereby made manifest. Is the Changes not that whereby the Sages fathom the profound? The subtle beginnings of movement and stillness are contained within the unfathomable—how incipient they are! Once the Sages established the images and transformations, what was incipient was thereby made evident. Is the Changes not that whereby the Sages investigate the incipient? Now, since the profound is fathomed through the explanations and prognostications, the explanations and prognostications themselves are profound…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而神矣幾研於象變則象變即幾而神矣唯深
故或吉或凶無昏民焉而天下之志以通唯幾
故以趨以避無僨事焉而天下之務以成唯神
故通若啓之成若相之而疾不待速行不待至
矣是辭占雖具於易而實因聖心之精以泄則
神於通志者謂非聖人之至精耶象變雖具於
易而實因聖心之變以顯則神於成務者謂非
聖人之至變耶信乎易有聖人之道四焉者此
之謂矣體易致用者其知聖人作易之功哉雖
===
然易非聖不能作亦非聖不能用蓋作以洗心
退藏用以齋戒神明非徒索之卦爻象數者此
道所以神而天下賴之寡過也彼太玄潛虛之
易視聖人爲何如
書
非知之艱行之惟艱王忱不艱允協于先
王成德惟說不言有厥咎
顧憲成
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔思致精深詞調醇雅〕
punctuated:
而神矣；幾研於象變，則象變即幾而神矣。唯深，故或吉或凶，無昏民焉，而天下之志以通；唯幾，故以趨以避，無僨事焉，而天下之務以成；唯神，故通若啓之，成若相之，而疾不待速，行不待至矣。是辭占雖具於《易》，而實因聖心之精以泄，則神於通志者，謂非聖人之至精耶？象變雖具於《易》，而實因聖心之變以顯，則神於成務者，謂非聖人之至變耶？信乎，「《易》有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂矣。體《易》致用者，其知聖人作《易》之功哉！雖然，《易》非聖不能作，亦非聖不能用。蓋作以洗心退藏，用以齋戒神明，非徒索之卦爻象數者。此道所以神，而天下賴之寡過也。彼《太玄》、《潛虛》之易，視聖人爲何如！

《書》
「非知之艱，行之惟艱。王忱不艱，允協于先王成德；惟說不言，有厥咎。」
顧憲成
同考試官教諭蔣　批：〔思致精深，詞調醇雅，〕
translation_en:
…and therefore numinous; when the subtle incipient tendencies are investigated through the images and changes, then those images and changes are themselves subtle and therefore numinous. Because it is profound, whether things bode good fortune or ill, the people are not left in confusion, and thus the intentions of all under heaven are penetrated; because it is subtle, in knowing what to pursue and what to avoid, affairs are not ruined, and thus the undertakings of all under heaven are brought to completion; because it is numinous, penetration comes as if opened for them and completion comes as if assisted for them, so that it is swift without waiting to hurry and arrives without waiting to travel. Thus, although the explanations and prognostications are contained in the Classic of Changes (Yi), they are in fact disclosed through the utmost refinement of the sages' minds—how then could that which is numinous in penetrating intentions be called anything other than the utmost refinement of the sages? And although the images and changes are contained in the Changes, they are in fact made manifest through the transformations of the sages' minds—how then could that which is numinous in completing undertakings be called anything other than the utmost transformation of the sages? Truly, when it is said that "the Changes contains the Way of the sages in four respects," this is what is meant! May those who embody the Changes and put it into practice recognize the achievement of the sages in composing the Changes! Even so, just as none but a sage could compose the Changes, so too none but a sage can truly use it. For its composition lay in cleansing the mind and withdrawing into hiddenness, and its use lies in fasting and vigilance to commune with the spiritual and luminous, not merely in seeking it among the hexagrams, lines, images, and numbers. This is why the Way is numinous, and why all under heaven rely upon it to lessen their faults. As for those "Changes" of the Canon of Supreme Mystery (Taixuan) and the Classic of Hidden Emptiness (Qianxu), how can they compare with the work of the sages?

Classic of Documents (Shu)
"It is not knowing that is difficult, but acting that is truly difficult. Since the King is sincerely not treating it as difficult, he will truly harmonize with the perfected virtue of the former kings; if I, Yue, were not to speak, the fault would be mine."
Gu Xiancheng 顧憲成
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Jiang: [His thought is refined and profound, his phrasing and cadence pure and elegant; …]

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
奇士也敬服敬服
同考試官教授黃　批〔詞淵意盲深得人臣告君之體觀此作足覘所蘊矣〕
考試官右賛善陳　批〔發揮明切〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔詞意婉曲明潤錄之〕
大臣期賢王力行之實而以言自信焉夫君德
協于先王此惟力行能之也大臣猶以不言爲
已咎斯責難之深意歟想其復于高宗蓋謂憲
天爲治臣言之而王以爲可行此可謂知矣然
===
知之者或不足于行知非所以爲難也行之者
必欲踐其知行始所以爲難也王誠以知爲不
可恃無徒激于所聞則定力與定志兼該將足
以上符乎先德之盛以言爲必可行不欲安于
所易則實意與實功並懋自可以遠追乎世德
之隆先王固有配天之至敬王能有法天之大
公先後其一揆也在先王能顧天之明命王亦
憲天之聰明創守爲一道也如是則王信能行
其所知矣惟說也不命其承圖夙所自許者敢
punctuated:
奇士也，敬服敬服。〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔詞淵意盲，深得人臣告君之體，觀此作足覘所蘊矣。〕
考試官右賛善陳　批〔發揮明切。〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔詞意婉曲明潤，錄之。〕
大臣期賢王力行之實，而以言自信焉。夫君德協于先王，此惟力行能之也；大臣猶以不言爲已咎，斯責難之深意歟？想其復于高宗，蓋謂憲天爲治，臣言之而王以爲可行，此可謂知矣。然知之者或不足于行，知非所以爲難也；行之者必欲踐其知，行始所以爲難也。王誠以知爲不可恃，無徒激于所聞，則定力與定志兼該，將足以上符乎先德之盛；以言爲必可行，不欲安于所易，則實意與實功並懋，自可以遠追乎世德之隆。先王固有配天之至敬，王能有法天之大公，先後其一揆也；在先王能顧天之明命，王亦憲天之聰明，創守爲一道也。如是，則王信能行其所知矣。惟說也，不命其承，圖夙所自許者，敢…
translation_en:
…He is an extraordinary scholar; I am filled with admiration, filled with admiration.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoshou) Huang comments: [The diction is deep and the meaning rich [?], thoroughly capturing the proper form of a minister addressing his sovereign. Viewing this piece suffices to glimpse the depth of what he holds within.]
Examiner, Right Admonisher (you zanshan) Chen comments: [The exposition is clear and incisive.]
Examiner, Left Companion (zuo zhongyun) Dai comments: [The diction and meaning are nuanced, clear, and polished; record it.]

The great minister looks to the worthy king for the substance of vigorous practice, while pledging himself to speak out. Now, for a sovereign's virtue to harmonize with that of the former kings is something that only vigorous practice can achieve; yet the great minister still regards any failure to speak as his own fault—is this not the profound intention of holding one's prince to the highest standards?

Reflecting on his reply to Gaozong, he meant to say: In taking Heaven as the model for governance, your servant has spoken of it and Your Majesty considers it practicable—this may be called knowing it. Yet those who know a thing may fall short in practicing it, so knowing is not what is difficult; those who practice it must seek to fulfill what they know in action, and only then does practice become what is difficult.

If Your Majesty truly regards mere knowledge as unreliable, and is not merely stirred of the moment by what you hear, then steadfast strength and steadfast resolve will both be encompassed, which will suffice to match above the flourishing virtue of the former kings. If you regard these words as something that must be put into practice, and do not wish to rest content with what is easy, then genuine intent and genuine achievement will advance together, whereby you can naturally rival from afar the exalted virtue of past generations. The former kings inherently possessed the utmost reverence that matched Heaven, and if Your Majesty can possess the great impartiality that models itself on Heaven, then earlier and later rulers will follow a single principle. The former kings were able to keep in view the bright mandate of Heaven, and if Your Majesty likewise takes as your model the intelligence and clarity of Heaven, then founding and preserving the dynasty will form a single Way. If it is thus, then Your Majesty will truly be able to put into practice what you know.

As for Yue, even before being commanded to take up my charge, I already aspired to this; now, would I dare…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不盡攄所聞以罄生平之願知之或不言也是
有君亦負之矣祇承于命正時之恐後者敢不
悉敷所得以答明主之知言之或不盡也是遭
時莫之効矣說何所辭其咎耶夫說之進言寔
賴王行言以啓之則力行以協德誠不容已矣
可但責言于臣哉抑納誨輔德說豈後言者必
德成始引爲己咎不亦晚乎是不然人主嘗感
激于聽言而忽意于實行古今大氐然也高宗
稱明哲矣當不至是說惓惓猶望之蓋益成其
===
德業爲己進言之地耳噫此有商令主賢臣世
世頌之不衰歟
其爾典常作之師
蔣瑞卿
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔此題作者類能言之非冗則略此篇盡刊陳言獨悉本意宛然周家之典常誠可爲多士式也〕
同考試官教授黃　批〔氣清詞雅字字句句皆不浮經義之可傳者〕
punctuated:
不盡攄所聞，以罄生平之願？知之或不言也，是有君亦負之矣；祇承于命，正時之恐後者，敢不悉敷所得，以答明主之知？言之或不盡也，是遭時莫之効矣。說何所辭其咎耶？夫說之進言，寔賴王行言以啓之，則力行以協德，誠不容已矣，可但責言于臣哉！抑納誨輔德，說豈後言者？必德成始引爲己咎，不亦晚乎？是不然。人主嘗感激于聽言，而忽意于實行，古今大氐然也。高宗稱明哲矣，當不至是。說惓惓猶望之，蓋益成其德業，爲己進言之地耳。噫！此有商令主賢臣，世世頌之不衰歟！

其爾典常作之師
蔣瑞卿
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔此題作者類能言之，非冗則略。此篇盡刊陳言，獨悉本意，宛然周家之典常，誠可爲多士式也。〕
同考試官教授黃　批〔氣清詞雅，字字句句皆不浮，經義之可傳者。〕
translation_en:
… not fully set forth what I have heard, so as to exhaust my lifelong aspiration? If I know something and perhaps do not speak, then even though I have such a ruler, I would be failing him. Reverently receiving Your charge—at a moment when I only fear falling behind—how could I dare not fully lay out what I have attained in order to answer the recognition of an enlightened sovereign? If I speak and perhaps do not say everything, then having met with the right moment, I would have rendered no service to it. How could I, Yue, excuse myself from that fault? Now, for Yue to offer counsel truly depends upon the King's putting words into action so as to open the way for it. Thus, striving in practice so as to harmonize with virtue truly admits of no cessation—how could one merely demand words from one's minister! Yet in accepting instruction to assist virtue, would Yue be one to hold back his words? To take the blame upon himself only after the King's virtue is already perfected—would that not be too late? It is not so. Rulers of men are often deeply moved when listening to counsel, yet careless in actual practice; past and present, it is generally thus. Gaozong is acclaimed as wise and discerning, and surely would not come to this; that Yue earnestly still hopes this of him is simply so as to further perfect his virtuous achievement and make room for his own offering of counsel. Ah! Is this not why the fine ruler and worthy minister of the Shang are praised without fail from generation to generation!

"Take your constant norms as your teacher." [Book of Documents, "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan)]
Jiang Ruiqing 蔣瑞卿
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Jiang: 〔Writers on this topic are generally able to say something about it, but if they are not prolix then they are sketchy. This essay completely trims away clichés and alone fully grasps the original meaning; it vividly captures the constant norms of the House of Zhou, and truly can serve as a model for the many scholars.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang: 〔The vital breath is clear and the diction elegant; not a single character or phrase is superficial. It is an exposition of the Classic worthy of being transmitted.〕

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官右贊善陳　批〔詞整意足〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔渾雅可錄〕
賢王訓官欲其遵王之制也夫周之典常王制
也於此師之而涖官之道有弗盡哉成王訓百
官之意謂夫王者之經世以法臣子之守法以
時學古而必議以制者非時也乃若周之典常
謨烈本于文武而丕顯丕承制作成于周公而
盡善盡美監古昔大猷之盛開萬年啓佑之功
此則宜于今而可師者也爾惟思典刑之具在
===
而是則是効法其不易之規仰彛典之大明而
不愆不忘遵爲畫一之守朝有道揆則論道者
師之參賛謨謀一因乎成憲而聰明非所用也
國有法守則奉法者師之阜成宣力悉考其舊
章而沿襲非所嫌也政固有以俗革者而文武
之政蓋酌風會氣化之流而通變以宜民者也
世方賴之以致治而守其成規不可永制于未
亂耶法固有以時變者而周公之法正觀人情
物理之極而更化以趨時者也國方賴之以乂
punctuated:
考試官右贊善陳批：〔詞整意足。〕
考試官左中允戴批：〔渾雅可錄。〕
賢王訓官，欲其遵王之制也。夫周之典常，王制也，於此師之，而涖官之道有弗盡哉？成王訓百官之意，謂夫王者之經世以法，臣子之守法以時，學古而必議以制者，非時也。乃若周之典常，謨烈本于文、武而丕顯丕承，制作成于周公而盡善盡美，監古昔大猷之盛，開萬年啓佑之功，此則宜于今而可師者也。爾惟思典刑之具在，而是則是効，法其不易之規；仰彛典之大明，而不愆不忘，遵爲畫一之守。朝有道揆，則論道者師之，參賛謨謀，一因乎成憲，而聰明非所用也；國有法守，則奉法者師之，阜成宣力，悉考其舊章，而沿襲非所嫌也。政固有以俗革者，而文、武之政，蓋酌風會氣化之流，而通變以宜民者也。世方賴之以致治，而守其成規，不可永制于未亂耶？法固有以時變者，而周公之法，正觀人情物理之極，而更化以趨時者也。國方賴之以乂…
translation_en:
Examiner Chen, Right Admonisher (you zanshan), comments: [The phrasing is well-ordered and the meaning is complete.]
Examiner Dai, Left Companion (zuo zhongyun), comments: [Profound and elegant; worthy of inclusion.]

When the worthy king instructed his officials, he wished them to abide by the king's institutions. Now, the constant norms of Zhou are the king's institutions; if one takes these as one's model, how could the way of administering office not be fully realized? The intent of King Cheng in instructing the hundred officials was to say that a true king orders the world through laws, and subjects and ministers uphold those laws in accordance with the times; to study antiquity and yet insist on deliberating over new institutions is out of step with the times. As for the constant norms of Zhou, their grand plans and glorious achievements were rooted in Kings Wen and Wu—greatly manifest and greatly carried forward—while their institutional creations were brought to completion by the Duke of Zhou—perfectly good and perfectly noble. Mirroring the flourishing of the great counsels of antiquity and inaugurating the merit of ten thousand years of enlightenment and protection, these are what suit the present and can be taken as a model. You should simply reflect on how the canonical models are all present here, taking them as your standard and emulating them, following their immutable rules; look up to the great brilliance of the constant statutes, neither erring nor forgetting, and abide by them with uniform observance. When the court has a measure of the Way, those who discourse on the Way take it as their model: in participating in and assisting with counsels and plans, they rely entirely on the established constitution, and personal cleverness is of no use. When the state has guardians of the law, those who uphold the law take them as their model: in bringing about abundance and exerting their strength, they examine all the old statutes, and following precedent is nothing to be shunned. Governance, to be sure, is sometimes reformed according to customs; yet the governance of Kings Wen and Wu weighed the currents of prevailing trends and cosmic transformations, adapting through change to suit the people. The world just now relies on this to achieve order—by preserving their established rules, can one not forever maintain control before disorder arises? Laws, to be sure, are sometimes altered according to the times; yet the laws of the Duke of Zhou observed the ultimate principles of human sentiment and the nature of things, renewing transformations to keep pace with the times. The state just now relies on this to bring about…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
安而稽其故實不可常保于不危耶如是則趨
向以端官常以肅欽司慎令莫是過矣爾其懋
哉嘗聞之有治人無治法得其人則準令可也
不狥令亦可也非其人則師心非也師法亦非
也不然周禮一書非不詳且備也而如歆如石
卒不能用以致治何哉此周禮周官相爲表裏
而志勤恭儉之戒成王所以深致意于用法之
人也
詩
關關雎鳩在河之洲窈窕淑女君子好逑
張後甲
===
同考試官教諭林　批〔太姒以德配德意發揮婉曲透麗深得風人之旨〕
同考試官教諭汪　批〔好逑意發得盡而且詞氣溫厚句法鏗鏘宜式多士〕
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔發好逑處無一閑字贅語一結尤知大義是邃于經學者〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔太姒和敬之德形容〕
punctuated:
安，而稽其故實，不可常保于不危耶？如是，則趨向以端，官常以肅，欽司慎令，莫是過矣！爾其懋哉！」嘗聞之：有治人，無治法。得其人，則準令可也，不狥令亦可也；非其人，則師心非也，師法亦非也。不然，《周禮》一書，非不詳且備也，而如歆、如石，卒不能用以致治，何哉？此《周禮》、《周官》相爲表裏，而「志勤恭儉」之戒，成王所以深致意于用法之人也。

《詩》
「關關雎鳩，在河之洲。窈窕淑女，君子好逑。」
張後甲
同考試官教諭林　批〔太姒以德配德意，發揮婉曲透麗，深得風人之旨。〕
同考試官教諭汪　批〔好逑意發得盡，而且詞氣溫厚，句法鏗鏘，宜式多士。〕
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔發好逑處，無一閑字贅語，一結尤知大義，是邃于經學者。〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔太姒和敬之德，形容〕
translation_en:
…and peace; by examining his established precedents, can we not perpetually preserve the state from peril? If you do this, then orientations will be rectified and official conduct will be made reverent; nothing surpasses this in respecting your duties and being cautious with ordinances! Exert yourselves in this!"

One has heard it said: "There are men who govern, not laws that govern." When the right men are found, conforming to the ordinances is acceptable, and not rigidly adhering to the ordinances is also acceptable; when the right men are not found, relying on one's own mind is wrong, and relying on the laws is also wrong. Otherwise, the book of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) is by no means lacking in detail and completeness, yet why was it that men like Liu Xin 劉歆 and Wang Anshi 王安石 ultimately could not use it to bring about good governance? This is how the Rites of Zhou and the "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan) serve as the outer and inner aspects of one another, and why, through the admonition to be "purposeful, diligent, respectful, and frugal," King Cheng 成王 directed his deepest attention to the men who implement the laws.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"Guan-guan cry the ospreys, on the islet of the river. Delicate and virtuous is the maiden, a good mate for the lord."
By Zhang Houjia 張後甲

Associate Examiner, Instructor Lin 林 comments: 〔The idea of Taisi 太姒 matching virtue with virtue is elaborated with subtle grace and penetrating beauty, deeply capturing the purport of the poet of the Airs.〕
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wang 汪 comments: 〔The meaning of "a good mate" is brought out to the fullest; moreover, the tone is gentle and generous and the phrasing resonant—fit to serve as a model for the many scholars.〕
Associate Examiner, Instructor Deng 鄧 comments: 〔Where it elaborates on "a good mate," there is not a single idle word or superfluous phrase; the conclusion especially shows an understanding of the great principle. This is someone profound in classical learning.〕
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔Taisi's virtues of harmony and reverence are depicted…〕

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
委蕭善體宮人好德之意者
考試官右賛善陳　批〔春容可誦〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔溫雅得旨〕
詩人與淑女之德克配乎君子焉蓋和敬閨門
之全德也淑女有焉其斯以為君子之善偶乎
詩人託興以美后妃者意謂人倫莫先於妃匹
而人道惟在於和敬吾茲於雎鳩而有感焉雄
鳴於前而雌則應之關關然於水中之洲其並
遊者若見其情之至而又未常狎也雌鳴於後
===
而雄則倡之關關然於河洲之上其定偶者若
見其類之別而又未甞離也吾故觀雎鳩而知
物之有善偶也况我淑女窈然其幽深而情欲
之感無所動於中窕然其閑雅而宴私之意無
所形於外徽柔如君子而以窈窕者承之則雍
雍乎其和者其情固足以相親也蓋和勝或近
於嫚而淑女則無之矣懿恭如君子而以窈窕
者承之則肅肅乎其敬者其禮又足以相別也
蓋敬勝或近於離而淑女則無之矣吾不圖君
punctuated:
〔委蕭，善體宮人好德之意者。〕
考試官右賛善陳　批〔春容可誦。〕
