If we observe the realm today: the four quarters are tranquil and peaceful, without the alarm of levying war chariots and registering cavalry horses; the regulations and statutes are complete, offering the convenience of moving…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
臂使指之便也非可謂清明之世哉海內
之士翕然嚮用求稱
上意凡蒿目而譚世持籌而畫計者豈少邪顧
其習大都在喜功立名耳功名者蓋臣執
以獻忱明主操以礪世兩必藉焉一切驟
禁而槩抑之將忠讜者避嫌宴安者藉口
非計之得也但天下之事成于好名而嘗
敗于好虛名起于喜功而多敝于無實功
不爲蚤辨情僞伏于微曖是非亂于疑似
===
其弊且以張大託之經世滑稽託之應變
儇利託之通權矯激託之勵節始以名溷
實終也實不可見并其名而掩之以此從
事譬絲紊舟而土埕之非不可觀而試之
江湖則甚危矣此所惡於虛名之士也當
今之計起而維之非槩責功名之士爲不
可亦豈令天下盡逃于功名之外哉天下
方競名以眩實吾然後據實以核名名實
辨而吏治飭矣是故蹟之著者旣顯然優
punctuated: 臂使指之便也，非可謂清明之世哉？海內之士翕然嚮用，求稱上意。凡蒿目而譚世、持籌而畫計者，豈少邪？顧其習大都在喜功立名耳。功名者，蓋臣執以獻忱，明主操以礪世，兩必藉焉。一切驟禁而槩抑之，將忠讜者避嫌，宴安者藉口，非計之得也。但天下之事，成于好名，而嘗敗于好虛名；起于喜功，而多敝于無實功。不爲蚤辨，情僞伏于微曖，是非亂于疑似。其弊且以張大託之經世，滑稽託之應變，儇利託之通權，矯激託之勵節。始以名溷實，終也實不可見，并其名而掩之。以此從事，譬絲紊舟而土埕之，非不可觀，而試之江湖則甚危矣。此所惡於虛名之士也。當今之計，起而維之，非槩責功名之士爲不可，亦豈令天下盡逃于功名之外哉？天下方競名以眩實，吾然後據實以核名。名實辨而吏治飭矣。是故蹟之著者，旣顯然優
translation_en: … the convenience of an arm commanding the fingers—can this not be called an era of clarity and peace? Gentlemen within the seas unanimously aspire to be employed, seeking to satisfy His Majesty's intentions. Are those who gaze anxiously over the world to discuss its affairs, or hold counting rods to devise plans, at all few in number? Yet their habit largely lies in delighting in achievements and establishing a name for themselves. Now, achievement and reputation are what a minister holds to offer his sincerity, and what an enlightened ruler wields to whet the age; both sides must rely upon them. If we abruptly prohibit everything and uniformly suppress them, then the loyal and forthright will avoid suspicion, while the indolent and comfort-seeking will find an excuse; this is not a sound plan. However, the affairs of the world succeed through a fondness for reputation, yet often fail through a fondness for empty reputation; they arise from delighting in achievements, yet mostly deteriorate from lacking real achievements. If one does not distinguish them early on, truth and falsehood will lurk in subtle obscurity, and right and wrong will be confounded by specious resemblances. The abuse will go so far that grandiloquence passes itself off as statecraft, glibness passes itself off as adaptability to change, nimble opportunism passes itself off as tactical flexibility, and perverse extremism passes itself off as moral integrity. At first, reputation confuses reality; in the end, reality cannot be seen, and even the reputation itself is obscured. To conduct affairs in this manner is like caulking a boat with tangled silk and plastering it with mud [?]: it is not unpleasant to look at, yet to test it upon rivers and lakes is perilous indeed! This is what is detested in men of empty reputation. The plan for the present day, in rising to uphold standards, is not to uniformly condemn men of achievement and reputation as unacceptable, nor is it to cause the whole world to flee entirely outside the realm of achievement and reputation. When the world is vying for reputation so as to dazzle reality, we then rely on reality to verify reputation. Once reputation and reality are distinguished, official administration will be put in order. Therefore, for those whose accomplishments are manifest, we already openly reward…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之矣而其心果實則雖不試之以身而事
幾未露豫有指授之功者不可沒也迹涉
可疑冒犯誹以爲之而計安社稷者尤當
諒也勞盡于此收功于彼而已不有其名
者不以掩也倡言獻議非有希覬卽未能
收後來之效勿詰也大節無玷雖細過瑕
疵可原也口不言功獨任事積勞者卽瑣
職下僚宜㧞也如此而實者有不辨乎業
之廢者固顯然黜之矣而心或非實則炫
===
才喜俠張虛聲而弗肩鉅遠者可勿用也
指陳世故若出于公而意在譸張以濟已
私者當遠也知難不救待旣變而收之以
邀己功者不足尚也崇論閎議尚自標榜
而卒墮行實者不可據也利在一時非
萬全之計而得失不相償者勿用也假恬
退鎭靜之名而實遷延觀望者可厭也如
此則不實者有不辨乎愚所陳責實之務
輕重于今日之勢者大較盖不出此矣顧
punctuated: 之矣。而其心果實，則雖不試之以身，而事幾未露、豫有指授之功者，不可沒也；迹涉可疑，冒犯誹以爲之，而計安社稷者，尤當諒也；勞盡于此，收功于彼，而已不有其名者，不以掩也；倡言獻議，非有希覬，卽未能收後來之效，勿詰也；大節無玷，雖細過瑕疵，可原也；口不言功，獨任事積勞者，卽瑣職下僚，宜㧞也。如此而實者有不辨乎？業之廢者，固顯然黜之矣。而心或非實，則炫才喜俠，張虛聲而弗肩鉅遠者，可勿用也；指陳世故，若出于公，而意在譸張以濟已私者，當遠也；知難不救，待旣變而收之以邀己功者，不足尚也；崇論閎議，尚自標榜，而卒墮行實者，不可據也；利在一時，非萬全之計，而得失不相償者，勿用也；假恬退鎭靜之名，而實遷延觀望者，可厭也。如此則不實者有不辨乎？愚所陳責實之務，輕重于今日之勢者，大較盖不出此矣。顧
translation_en:
… [openly reward] them. And if their hearts are truly substantive, then even if they have not tested something in person, those who have the merit of giving advance direction before the signs of an affair have become visible must not be overlooked; those whose actions appear suspicious and who brave slander to carry them out, yet whose plans secure the altars of state, ought especially to be understood and excused; those who exhaust their toil here while the success is reaped there, without claiming the reputation for themselves, should not have their merit obscured; those who initiate proposals and offer counsel without ulterior ambitions should not be censured even if their proposals fail to achieve subsequent results; those whose great integrity is unblemished may be forgiven despite minor faults and blemishes; and those who never speak of their own merit, yet shoulder responsibilities alone and accumulate toil, ought to be promoted even if they are in petty posts and lowly offices. In this way, will any who are substantive fail to be distinguished?

Those whose duties are neglected are, of course, openly dismissed. Yet if their hearts lack substance, then those who flaunt their talent and delight in bravado, spreading empty renown while refusing to shoulder great and far-reaching responsibilities, should not be employed; those who point out and set forth worldly affairs as though acting out of public spirit, yet whose intent is to deceive and exaggerate in order to further their own private interests, ought to be kept at a distance; those who perceive a crisis and do not rescue it, waiting until disaster has struck to step in and claim the credit for themselves, are not worthy of esteem; those who indulge in lofty discourses and grand arguments, prizing self-promotion while ultimately ruining practical conduct, cannot be relied upon; those whose measures bring only momentary profit rather than a completely sound plan, where the gains do not compensate for the losses, should not be adopted; and those who borrow the name of calm modesty and quiet composure, while in reality procrastinating and waiting to see how the wind blows, are detestable. In this way, will any who lack substance fail to be distinguished?

What I, in my humble folly, have set forth regarding the task of demanding substance, weighing the relative priorities in light of today's circumstances, generally does not go beyond this. Yet…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
惟係
上之所倡焉譬之音鼓宮而宮應鼓角而角應
者也夫天下豪賢固不少而中才嘗多盖
闕
上意嚮以爲轉移者非
聖人南面而立鏡覽燭照握其柄而默化之則
賢否一區眞贗一途無論中才卽豪賢者
且將遷就于其間矣此愚所云辨之不可
不蚤也辨之蚤則凡天下之以名至者知
吾必察其實惟恐名聞于上以蹈虛浮之
罰而競功營職不暇矣一意念所及則以
正士習何習不正以飭吏治何治不飭而
挽回今日之勢者是或一道矣乎不此之
務泄泄然承舛襲訛謂可毋擾或朝議法
而暮改制以駭愕聽睹者則非愚生所及
知也
第五問
陸起龍
punctuated:
惟係上之所倡焉。譬之音，鼓宮而宮應，鼓角而角應者也。夫天下豪賢固不少，而中才嘗多，盖闚上意嚮以爲轉移者。非聖人南面而立，鏡覽燭照，握其柄而默化之，則賢否一區，眞贗一途，無論中才，卽豪賢者且將遷就于其間矣。此愚所云辨之不可不蚤也。辨之蚤，則凡天下之以名至者，知吾必察其實，惟恐名聞于上以蹈虛浮之罰，而競功營職不暇矣。一意念所及，則以正士習，何習不正？以飭吏治，何治不飭？而挽回今日之勢者，是或一道矣乎！不此之務，泄泄然承舛襲訛，謂可毋擾，或朝議法而暮改制，以駭愕聽睹者，則非愚生所及知也。

第五問
陸起龍
translation_en:
…solely depends on what the Sovereign initiates. It is comparable to musical tones: strike the gong note and the gong responds; strike the jue note and the jue responds. Now, while heroic and worthy men in the world are certainly not few, men of middling talent are always in the majority; they are the ones who peer at the Sovereign's inclinations and shift themselves accordingly. Unless the Sage stands facing south, surveying like a mirror and illuminating like a torch, holding fast the handle of authority and transforming them imperceptibly, then the worthy and the unworthy will be grouped together, the genuine and the counterfeit will share the same path, and to say nothing of those of middling talent, even the heroic and worthy will begin to compromise and accommodate themselves among them. This is why I say that distinguishing between them must be done early. If the distinction is made early, then all in the world who come forward on the strength of their reputation will know that we will certainly investigate their reality; they will only fear that their mere reputation might reach the Sovereign and incur the punishment for empty superficiality, and thus they will scarcely have enough time to strive for real achievements and attend to their duties. Once this single intention reaches everywhere, then if used to rectify the habits of scholars, what habit will not be rectified? If used to put in order the administration of officials, what administration will not be put in order? To reverse the tendencies of the present day, might this not be the one true way? As for neglecting this task—either sluggishly perpetuating errors and following mistakes under the pretext of avoiding disturbance, or debating laws in the morning and altering regulations in the evening so as to startle what people hear and see—that is beyond what this foolish student is able to comprehend.

Fifth Question
Lu Qilong 陸起龍

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官推官史　批〔條答時務纚纚數百千言悉中肯綮且謂振紀綱在先正風俗尤知〕
〔要之論子所謂俊傑者非耶錄之〕
考試官右贊善陳　批〔經生搦管譚時務而論議剴切皆此蓋亦夙抱忠讜者〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔剖答時務甚當必究心經濟之士也宜錄〕
治天下若理身然身之偶失其理也有發
於支體徵於顏色者顯而易見者也所謂
標也有運於氣候行於脉理者隱而難知
者也所謂本也善醫者固不敢以迂緩之
見而遺其標亦不敢以欲速之心而傷其
本故藥石鍼砭固所必用而調和保護尤
有獨重者夫是以標與本皆理而身隨以
安也通於此說者可以語時務矣生也草
野跧伏徒操筴習爲章句耳而執事以俊
傑期之非所敢承也然亦豈敢虛明問而
不一陳其愚乎夫北虜貪暴無親舊矣乃
punctuated:
同考試官推官史　批〔條答時務，纚纚數百千言，悉中肯綮；且謂振紀綱在先正風俗，尤知要之論。子所謂俊傑者非耶？錄之。〕
考試官右贊善陳　批〔經生搦管譚時務，而論議剴切皆此，蓋亦夙抱忠讜者。〕
考試官左中允戴　批〔剖答時務甚當，必究心經濟之士也，宜錄。〕

治天下若理身然。身之偶失其理也，有發於支體、徵於顏色者，顯而易見者也，所謂標也；有運於氣候、行於脉理者，隱而難知者也，所謂本也。善醫者固不敢以迂緩之見而遺其標，亦不敢以欲速之心而傷其本。故藥石鍼砭固所必用，而調和保護尤有獨重者。夫是以標與本皆理，而身隨以安也。通於此說者，可以語時務矣。生也草野跧伏，徒操筴習爲章句耳，而執事以俊傑期之，非所敢承也。然亦豈敢虛明問而不一陳其愚乎？夫北虜貪暴無親，舊矣。乃
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge Shi, comments: 〔He responds point by point to current affairs in hundreds and thousands of flowing words, all hitting the mark; moreover, his claim that invigorating discipline and order lies first in rectifying customs is an argument that especially grasps the essentials. Is this gentleman not what one calls an outstanding talent? Record it.〕
Examiner, Right Admonisher Chen, comments: 〔When a student of the classics takes up his brush to discuss current affairs and his arguments are all as trenchant and pertinent as this, he must be one who has long harbored loyalty and forthrightness.〕
Examiner, Left Companion Dai, comments: 〔His analysis and answers regarding current affairs are very fitting; he must be a scholar who devotes his mind to statecraft. It ought to be recorded.〕

Governing the realm is like regulating the body. When the body occasionally loses its proper regulation, there are conditions that break out in the limbs and manifest in the complexion; these are obvious and easy to see, and are what we call the branches (symptoms). There are also those that circulate in the vital breaths and move through the vessels; these are hidden and difficult to know, and are what we call the root. A skilled physician certainly dares not neglect the branches out of a迂緩 (circuitous and slow) view, nor dares he harm the root out of a desire for quick results. Therefore, while herbal medicines and stone or metal acupuncture needles must certainly be used, harmonizing and protecting are given particular weight. Thus, both the branches and the root are regulated, and the body accordingly becomes secure. One who understands this explanation can be spoken with about current affairs. I, a student crouching in the rustic wilds, merely hold my divination stalks and practice chapter-and-verse studies; that Your Excellency expects of me the qualities of an outstanding talent is not something I dare accept. Yet how could I dare leave your enlightened inquiry unanswered and fail to set forth my humble views for once? Now, that the Northern Caitiffs (Mongols) are greedy, violent, and without affection is an old story. Yet…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
一旦稱臣求市自我中國視之亦聖人之
所謂無故者也豺狼之欲稍不愜能保其
不沸唇相譙乎唐尚結賛之紿馬燧渾瑊
可監也漁陽突騎稱勁於天下夂矣且與
虜甚習而何至取辦於南兵乎遠調南兵
則不得不厚其廩食以少慰其意而欲得
虜情則凡偵視間諜衝鋒斷後諸勞役又
不得不用北兵之習於邊者吾恐南兵日
驕而北兵日憤矣唐涇原戍卒見神策衣
===
糧而愠曰人給五十千而不識戰鬭彼何
人耶常額衣資不給而前冐白刃此何人
耶雖以李光顏之忠義爲之將而幾不能
定可監也
國家財賦悉仰東南而漕渠阻則都市有脫
巾之虞邊儲專籍鹽課而鹽法壞則塞下
無可積之粟是數者誠當今之急務夫人
而知慮之也而愚猶以爲天下之安危未
盡在此何者我
punctuated: 一旦稱臣求市，自我中國視之，亦聖人之所謂「無故」者也。豺狼之欲稍不愜，能保其不沸唇相譙乎？唐尚結賛之紿馬燧、渾瑊，可監也。漁陽突騎稱勁於天下夂矣，且與虜甚習，而何至取辦於南兵乎？遠調南兵，則不得不厚其廩食以少慰其意；而欲得虜情，則凡偵視、間諜、衝鋒、斷後諸勞役，又不得不用北兵之習於邊者。吾恐南兵日驕而北兵日憤矣。唐涇原戍卒見神策衣糧而愠曰：「人給五十千而不識戰鬭，彼何人耶？常額衣資不給而前冐白刃，此何人耶？」雖以李光顏之忠義爲之將，而幾不能定，可監也。國家財賦悉仰東南，而漕渠阻，則都市有脫巾之虞；邊儲專籍鹽課，而鹽法壞，則塞下無可積之粟。是數者，誠當今之急務，夫人而知慮之也。而愚猶以爲天下之安危未盡在此。何者？我
translation_en:
… one day they declare themselves vassals and request border markets—viewed from the perspective of our Middle Kingdom, this too is what the Sage called a matter arising "without cause." If the desires of these jackals and wolves are even slightly unsatisfied, how can we guarantee that they will not clamor and berate us with boiling lips? In the Tang dynasty, how Shang Jiezan 尚結賛 deceived Ma Sui 馬燧 and Hun Jian 渾瑊 serves as a warning! The charging cavalry of Yuyang 漁陽 have long been renowned throughout the realm for their strength, and moreover they are thoroughly familiar with the northern caitiffs; why then must we rely on southern troops to handle the matter? When southern troops are transferred from afar, one cannot help but give them generous rations and provisions to somewhat soothe their feelings; yet when one wishes to ascertain the caitiffs' situation, for all such arduous tasks as scouting, espionage, charging the vanguard, and guarding the rear, one cannot help but employ northern troops who are accustomed to the frontier. I fear that the southern troops will grow more arrogant by the day while the northern troops grow more resentful by the day. In the Tang dynasty, when the garrison soldiers of Jingyuan 涇原 saw the clothing and grain of the Divine Strategy (Shence 神策) Army, they grew indignant and said: "Each man is given fifty thousand cash and yet knows nothing of combat—what sort of men are they? Our regular allowance of clothing and supplies is not even provided, and yet we go forward to brave naked blades—what sort of men are we?" Even with a commander of the loyalty and righteousness of Li Guangyan 李光顏 leading them, the mutiny could scarcely be quelled; this too serves as a warning!

The state's revenue and taxes depend entirely on the southeast, so if the Grand Canal is obstructed, the capital faces the danger of soldiers casting off their headscarves in mutiny; frontier provisions rely exclusively on the salt tax, so if the salt regulations break down, there is no grain that can be stockpiled along the borders. These several matters are truly urgent tasks of the present day, and every man knows to be concerned about them. Yet in my foolishness I still consider that the security and peril of the realm do not lie entirely in these things. Why is that? Our…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
國家之德澤深於殷周而威靈過於漢唐北
虜之不能難我中國也固天時亦人事然
也今業已通市矣誠堅彼之信約而又峻
我之隄防則吾自有以待之而虜之叛服
不足計也昔東南之有事也嘗調發燕趙
之兵矣卒所以成殄賊之功者南兵也然
則北邊之備又豈獨藉於南哉誠選塞下
之驍銳而以養南兵之費養之則北兵自
足以禦虜而南兵固可旦夕罷也若漕渠
===
之阻特當事者因循歲月不早濬其流於
未淤之先而又畏難苟且不務約其流於
既漫之後耳卽河竟難治而漕遂阻也如
漢唐之都長安漕不經砥柱險乎宋之都
汴梁不三倉轉運而江船不入淮淮船不
入江乎何必如今日之一水達都邑而後
可以爲國也鹽法一壞於輸粟之改銀再
壞於課價之日增今改者旣不可復而增
者又不可減則理鹽固以無善策矣卽鹽
punctuated: 國家之德澤深於殷、周，而威靈過於漢、唐。北虜之不能難我中國也，固天時，亦人事然也。今業已通市矣，誠堅彼之信約，而又峻我之隄防，則吾自有以待之，而虜之叛服不足計也。昔東南之有事也，嘗調發燕、趙之兵矣，卒所以成殄賊之功者，南兵也。然則北邊之備，又豈獨藉於南哉？誠選塞下之驍銳，而以養南兵之費養之，則北兵自足以禦虜，而南兵固可旦夕罷也。若漕渠之阻，特當事者因循歲月，不早濬其流於未淤之先，而又畏難苟且，不務約其流於既漫之後耳。卽河竟難治，而漕遂阻也，如漢、唐之都長安，漕不經砥柱險乎？宋之都汴梁，不三倉轉運，而江船不入淮，淮船不入江乎？何必如今日之一水達都邑，而後可以爲國也？鹽法一壞於輸粟之改銀，再壞於課價之日增。今改者旣不可復，而增者又不可減，則理鹽固以無善策矣。卽鹽
translation_en: …dynasty's virtuous beneficence is deeper than that of the Yin and Zhou, and its awesome authority surpasses that of the Han and Tang. That the northern caitiffs cannot trouble our Central Kingdom is indeed due to Heaven's timing, yet also to human affairs. Now that border markets have already been opened, if we truly hold firm to their treaties of good faith while also strengthening our own defenses, then we will naturally have the means to deal with them, and whether the caitiffs rebel or submit will not be worth reckoning. In the past, when there were disturbances in the southeast, troops from Yan and Zhao were once mobilized and dispatched; yet in the end, those who achieved the merit of exterminating the bandits were southern troops. This being so, how could the defense of the northern frontier depend solely upon the south? If we truly select the valiant and銳 (elite) soldiers along the frontier and support them with the funds used to maintain the southern troops, then the northern troops will naturally suffice to resist the caitiffs, and the southern troops can certainly be dismissed at short notice. As for the obstruction of the Grand Canal, it is merely that those in charge have temporized through the months and years, failing to dredge its current early before it silted up, and then, shrinking from difficulty and seeking momentary ease, failing to strive to constrain its flow after it had already overflowed. Even supposing the Yellow River ultimately proves difficult to control and grain transport is consequently blocked—when the Han and Tang made their capital at Chang'an, did their grain transport not pass through the perils of Mount Dizhu? When the Song made its capital at Bianliang, did they not use three granaries for relay transport, so that Yangtze boats did not enter the Huai and Huai boats did not enter the Yangtze? Why must a single waterway reach the capital directly, as it does today, before one can govern the state? The salt administration was first ruined when the delivery of grain was commuted to silver, and ruined a second time as the price of salt quotas increased daily. Now, since what was commuted cannot be restored, and what was increased cannot be reduced, there is indeed no good policy left for managing the salt monopoly. Yet even if the salt…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
利之失羸也不見文景之恭儉即未榷鹽
而國用饒武帝之侈肆即榷鹽而海內耗
乎何必邊儲之遂無以爲計也愚所竊憂
者十數年來法度之修改弊壞之搜剔幾
無纖芥之遺固求以富吾民耳而民猶未
見其加富也然諸言釐弊者猶未已則民
之日趣於窮也固未知其所極也自古天
潢之派未有如我
朝之盛者亦未有如我
===
朝之無事而坐食者今歲祿不支而待哺嗷
嗷者亦既久矣且其間豈無奇傑之才欲
如士民之效用者哉既無所用其才而又
無以資其生竊懼其一旦而有不可言者
也乃不此之慮而惟彼之憂蓋膚臂股之
病腫而忘疽之將發於背也至於紀綱風
俗則尤有難於言者夫張其大統之謂綱
理其小目之謂紀上之所以使乎下而成
臂指之勢者此也上行下效謂之風衆心
punctuated: 利之失羸也，不見文、景之恭儉，即未榷鹽而國用饒；武帝之侈肆，即榷鹽而海內耗乎？何必邊儲之遂無以為計也。愚所竊憂者，十數年來，法度之修改，弊壞之搜剔，幾無纖芥之遺，固求以富吾民耳，而民猶未見其加富也。然諸言釐弊者猶未已，則民之日趣於窮也，固未知其所極也。自古天潢之派，未有如我朝之盛者，亦未有如我朝之無事而坐食者。今歲祿不支，而待哺嗷嗷者，亦既久矣。且其間豈無奇傑之才，欲如士民之效用者哉？既無所用其才，而又無以資其生，竊懼其一旦而有不可言者也。乃不此之慮，而惟彼之憂，蓋膚臂股之病腫，而忘疽之將發於背也。至於紀綱、風俗，則尤有難於言者。夫張其大統之謂綱，理其小目之謂紀，上之所以使乎下而成臂指之勢者，此也；上行下效謂之風，眾心…
translation_en: …profits lose their surplus: do you not see that through the reverent frugality of Emperors Wen and Jing [of the Han], even without a salt monopoly, state finances were abundant; whereas through the extravagance and license of Emperor Wu, even with a salt monopoly, the realm within the seas was exhausted? Why must it be that frontier provisions are thereby left with no way to be planned for? What I privately worry about is that for the past十-odd years, the revision of laws and regulations and the rooting out of abuses and corruptions have left almost not the slightest bit overlooked. This was surely meant to enrich our people, yet the people still have not been seen to grow any richer. Even so, those who speak of reforming abuses have still not ceased; thus, as the people daily hasten toward destitution, one truly does not know where it will end. Since antiquity, the branches of the imperial clan have never been as flourishing as in our Dynasty, nor have they ever been as idle and living off stipends without duties as in our Dynasty. Now, for a long time already, their annual stipends have gone unpaid, and they have been crying out in hunger waiting to be fed. Moreover, among them how could there fail to be men of extraordinary and outstanding talent who wish to render service like the scholars and commoners? Since there is no way to employ their talents, and furthermore nothing with which to support their livelihood, I privately fear that one day something unspeakable may happen. Yet people do not give thought to this, and worry only about those other matters—this is like suffering from swelling in the skin, arms, and thighs while forgetting the carbuncle that is about to erupt on the back. As for state discipline and popular customs, there are things even more difficult to speak of. Stretching out the great main cord is called the headrope (gang), and ordering the small meshes is called the net-threads (ji); this is the means by which superiors command inferiors and form the dynamic of the arm directing the fingers. What superiors practice and inferiors imitate is called wind (feng), and the minds of the multitude…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
安定謂之俗下之所以戴乎上而成膠結
之理者此也自古有國家者其治未有不
由紀綱之振而風俗淳其亂亦未有不由
紀綱頹而風俗壞然惟紀綱不振而後風
俗漸壞亦由風俗旣壞而紀綱愈以不振
二者固交相病也方今
朝廷之政部院下之司府而司府下之州縣
無不承也謂紀綱之不整肅可乎顧上下
之所以相應者特在簿書之間爲名而已
===
矣上有所建置而姑待下之融通下有所
奉行而徐俟上之定議於是展轉支吾而
稽核奏報粲然無惑蓋往往功罪已明賞
罰已舉而究其國事之利病則猶夫故耳
方今天下之俗家慕乎章縫而人習乎弦
誦無不勸也謂風俗之不齊一也可乎顧
上下之所以相化者特在言貌之末爲文
而已矣上以道敎而不愧其身之不能先
下以道學而不羞其心之不能副於是因
punctuated: 安定謂之俗，下之所以戴乎上而成膠結之理者此也。自古有國家者，其治未有不由紀綱之振而風俗淳，其亂亦未有不由紀綱頹而風俗壞。然惟紀綱不振，而後風俗漸壞；亦由風俗旣壞，而紀綱愈以不振。二者固交相病也。方今朝廷之政，部院下之司府，而司府下之州縣，無不承也，謂紀綱之不整肅可乎？顧上下之所以相應者，特在簿書之間，爲名而已矣。上有所建置，而姑待下之融通；下有所奉行，而徐俟上之定議。於是展轉支吾，而稽核奏報粲然無惑。蓋往往功罪已明，賞罰已舉，而究其國事之利病，則猶夫故耳。方今天下之俗，家慕乎章縫，而人習乎弦誦，無不勸也，謂風俗之不齊一也可乎？顧上下之所以相化者，特在言貌之末，爲文而已矣。上以道敎，而不愧其身之不能先；下以道學，而不羞其心之不能副。於是因
translation_en:
… and when the hearts of the multitude are settled and stable, it is called custom (su). It is by this means that those below revere those above and form an indissoluble bond. Since antiquity, among those who have possessed states and families, there has never been a time of order that did not arise from the invigoration of discipline and order (jigang) and the purity of customs, nor has there been a time of disorder that did not arise from the decay of discipline and order and the corruption of customs. Yet it is only when discipline and order are not invigorated that customs gradually deteriorate; and likewise, once customs have deteriorated, discipline and order become all the more listless. The two indeed afflict each other mutually.

At present, in the governance of the Imperial Court, the Ministries and Censorate hand down orders to the Provincial Administrations and Prefectures, and the Provincial Administrations and Prefectures hand them down to the Subprefectures and Counties, with none failing to comply. Could one say that discipline and order are not well-regulated and strict? However, the way superiors and inferiors respond to one another exists merely among registers and documents, for the sake of name alone. When superiors establish a measure, they tentatively wait for those below to adapt and accommodate it; when inferiors carry out an order, they slowly wait for those above to settle their deliberations. Thereupon they shift back and forth and prevaricate, while the audits and memorialized reports appear brilliantly clear and beyond doubt. Thus, time and again, merits and offenses have already been clarified, and rewards and punishments have already been enacted, yet if one examines the actual benefits and harms to state affairs, they remain just as they were before.

At present, in the customs of the realm, every household admires the attire of the Confucian scholar, and every person practices singing to strings and reciting texts, with none failing to be encouraged. Could one say that customs are not uniform? However, the way superiors and inferiors transform one another exists merely in the superficialities of speech and demeanor, for the sake of outward ornament alone. Those above instruct by means of the Way, yet feel no shame that they cannot lead by personal example; those below study the Way, yet feel no disgrace that their hearts cannot match it in reality. Thereupon, through…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
緣附會而賛揚指摘翕然無二蓋往往優
劣已昭臧否已定而究其人品之賢不肖
則猶夫故耳夫是二者皆無弊壞之形而
陰有弊壞之漸故愚以爲前數者之可憂
所謂發於支體而徵於顔色人所共見也
此二者之可慮所謂運於氣候而行於脉
理人所未覺也不憂其所共見則歲侵月
削或至難支而不先理其所未覺則潛消
默耗可憂者將日以愈甚也然今
===
明天子獨攬乾綱容勿之臣悉忠而謀斷政柄
非有移也而紀綱猶未甚肅者正以風俗
爲之累耳愚以爲欲正今之風俗必塞其
功利之門而後可也夫
國家設官分職而豐祿以養之豈直使之無
所事事哉而在位諸臣薄著勞勩卽小者
望遷秩大者望叙蔭矣是以諸言興革者
紛紜未已彼非誠能爲生民憂社稷計也
大抵欲樹已之顯名而食其厚利也故筮
punctuated: 緣附會，而賛揚指摘，翕然無二。蓋往往優劣已昭，臧否已定，而究其人品之賢不肖，則猶夫故耳。夫是二者，皆無弊壞之形，而陰有弊壞之漸。故愚以爲前數者之可憂，所謂發於支體而徵於顔色，人所共見也；此二者之可慮，所謂運於氣候而行於脉理，人所未覺也。不憂其所共見，則歲侵月削，或至難支；而不先理其所未覺，則潛消默耗，可憂者將日以愈甚也。然今明天子獨攬乾綱，容勿之臣悉忠而謀斷，政柄非有移也，而紀綱猶未甚肅者，正以風俗爲之累耳。愚以爲欲正今之風俗，必塞其功利之門而後可也。夫國家設官分職，而豐祿以養之，豈直使之無所事事哉？而在位諸臣，薄著勞勩，卽小者望遷秩，大者望叙蔭矣。是以諸言興革者，紛紜未已，彼非誠能爲生民憂、社稷計也，大抵欲樹已之顯名，而食其厚利也。故筮
translation_en:
…they latch onto connections and force interpretations, so that in their praise and criticism they are in complete unanimity. Thus, time and again, superiority and inferiority are already made clear and judgments of good and bad are already settled, yet if one examines whether their personal character is truly worthy or unworthy, it remains just as it was before. Now, these two matters both lack the outward form of decay, yet secretly harbor the gradual tendency toward decay. Therefore, I humbly believe that the reasons the several former matters are cause for worry are like ailments that break out in the limbs and show in the complexion, which everyone can see; whereas the reasons these latter two are cause for concern are like ailments that circulate in the vital breaths and travel through the vessels and tissues, which people do not yet perceive. If we do not worry about what everyone sees, then as it erodes year by year and month by month, it may become impossible to sustain; yet if we do not first treat what is not yet perceived, then as it secretly wastes and silently consumes us, what is cause for worry will grow worse by the day.

However, at present our enlightened Son of Heaven holds sole grasp of the sovereign authority, and his trusted, diligent ministers are all loyal in their counsel and decisions. The handle of governance has not shifted elsewhere, and the reason state discipline is still not entirely strict is precisely that prevailing customs encumber it. I humbly believe that if we wish to rectify today's customs, we must first block the gate of utilitarian gain before it can be done. Now, when the state establishes offices, divides responsibilities, and nourishes officials with generous emoluments, is it merely to let them have nothing to do? Yet as soon as the various officials in office show some slight toil and merit, in lesser cases they hope for promotion in rank, and in greater cases they hope for hereditary privilege for their descendants. For this reason, those who propose initiatives or abolitions do so in endless profusion. They are not genuinely able to worry for the common people or plan for the altars of soil and grain; for the most part, they wish to establish an illustrious name for themselves and reap rich rewards from it. Thus, when they first enter…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
仕之初猶多修謹而既位通顯即生平故
態或暴露不諱彼其功利之欲已塞而無
所復覬也今宜明示
朝廷德意務在與民休息謹守舊法不爲煩
擾諸上章言事者一切報罷使人不復得
以窺其好惡之端而諸非有奇偉殊功僅
免瘝曠者舉不得議功而論賞則庶乎倖
進者寢謀而釣名飾貌之僞漸衰夫然後
衆皆安官樂職莫敢有苟且之意而紀綱
可得而舉也蓋功利息則衆知義衆知義
則必慮久遠而官職舉官職舉則
===
朝政行而諸可憂者次第修之無難矣猶人
身脉調氣暢而諸疾自平也昔漢王嘉言
漢家故事尚書爲希下章煩擾百姓宋李
沆言中外所陳利害或徇其請輕行一事
即所傷多矣嗚呼此漢文景宋真仁所以
培數百年國脉也哉愚生草茅之見未知
大體執事進而教之則幸矣
punctuated: 仕之初，猶多修謹；而既位通顯，即生平故態或暴露不諱。彼其功利之欲已塞，而無所復覬也。今宜明示朝廷德意，務在與民休息，謹守舊法，不爲煩擾。諸上章言事者，一切報罷，使人不復得以窺其好惡之端；而諸非有奇偉殊功、僅免瘝曠者，舉不得議功而論賞。則庶乎倖進者寢謀，而釣名飾貌之僞漸衰。夫然後衆皆安官樂職，莫敢有苟且之意，而紀綱可得而舉也。蓋功利息則衆知義，衆知義則必慮久遠而官職舉，官職舉則朝政行，而諸可憂者次第修之無難矣。猶人身脉調氣暢，而諸疾自平也。昔漢王嘉言：「漢家故事，尚書爲希下章，煩擾百姓。」宋李沆言：「中外所陳利害，或徇其請，輕行一事，即所傷多矣。」嗚呼！此漢文、景，宋真、仁所以培數百年國脉也哉！愚生草茅之見，未知大體，執事進而教之，則幸矣。
translation_en: …first enter officialdom, they are often still self-restrained and circumspect; yet once they reach prominent and exalted positions, their lifelong habitual faults are sometimes exposed without scruple. That is because their desires for merit and profit have already been satisfied, and they have nothing further to covet. Now it is fitting to clearly manifest the benevolent intentions of the Court, making it the priority to allow the people to rest and recuperate, carefully observing the established laws and creating no vexatious disturbances. As for all those who submit memorials to speak on affairs, let their proposals be uniformly set aside, so that men are no longer able to spy out the hints of the ruler's likes and dislikes; and as for all those who do not possess extraordinary and distinguished achievements, but have merely avoided negligence and dereliction of duty, let none of them be considered for merit or evaluated for rewards. Then perhaps those who seek advancement through luck will abandon their schemes, and the hypocrisy of fishing for fame and putting on false appearances will gradually decline. Only then will everyone be content in their offices and take pleasure in their duties, none daring to harbor perfunctory intentions, and the laws and discipline of the state can be upheld. For when the pursuit of merit and profit ceases, the multitude knows righteousness; when the multitude knows righteousness, they will surely take thought for the distant future and official duties will be properly discharged; when official duties are properly discharged, the administration of the Court will function effectively, and all the matters that cause concern can be rectified in sequence without difficulty. It is just like the human body: when the pulse is regulated and the vital breath flows smoothly, all ailments subside of their own accord. In former times, Wang Jia 王嘉 of the Han said, "According to the precedents of the Han house, the Masters of Writing rarely sent down memorials, lest they trouble and disturb the common people." Li Hang 李沆 of the Song said, "Regarding the advantages and disadvantages set forth by officials at court and in the provinces, if one accedes to their requests and lightly puts even a single matter into effect, the harm done is great indeed." Alas! Was this not the very means by which Emperors Wen 文 and Jing 景 of the Han, and Emperors Zhenzong 真宗 and Renzong 仁宗 of the Song, nurtured the vital pulse of the state for several hundred years! Such are the rustic views of this foolish student, who does not yet understand the grand principles of governance; should Your Excellencies bring me forward and instruct me, I would be fortunate indeed.

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
臣不佞載筆史署伏睹
詔旨求賢責實歲且屢下夫以寓
內之大士鱗集
輦轂者無限何致重釐
宸慮若此竊咨咨嘆焉今者猥承
上命校士南畿畀以網羅英俊之
===
寄則幸殊遘矣臣伏自念顧
安得盡賢士實與華稱也者
而
獻之備
上所驅策哉誠有其人而臣弗克
知遺于所舉之外如報塞何
故自受
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序
臣不佞，載筆史署，伏睹詔旨，求賢責實，歲且屢下。夫以寓內之大，士鱗集輦轂者無限，何致重釐宸慮若此？竊咨咨嘆焉。今者猥承上命，校士南畿，畀以網羅英俊之寄，則幸殊遘矣。臣伏自念，顧安得盡賢士實與華稱也者，而獻之備上所驅策哉？誠有其人，而臣弗克知，遺于所舉之外，如報塞何？故自受
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

Your unworthy servant, wielding the brush in the Historiography Institute, has humbly observed that imperial edicts seeking worthy men and demanding substantive results have been handed down repeatedly within the year. Given the vastness of the realm and the limitless number of scholars gathering like fish scales at the imperial capital, how has it come to burden the Emperor's thoughts so heavily? In private, I sighed over this again and again. Now, having unworthily received His Majesty's command to examine the scholars in the Southern Metropolitan Region, entrusted with the charge of gathering heroes and talents into the net, I am fortunate to have met with an extraordinary opportunity. Humbly reflecting to myself, how, though, can I obtain only worthy scholars whose substance matches their literary brilliance, and present them to be ready for His Majesty's employment? If there truly are such men, and your servant fails to recognize them, leaving them outside the ranks of those recommended, how could I fulfill my duty in repayment? Therefore, ever since receiving…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
命以來亦惟與共事之臣夙夜兢
惕思竭其駑下仰副
上意及握士所爲文讀之言若人
人殊類能發抒其所素蓄以
不詭于六經之旨臣盱衡擊
節不可勝收庶哉賢士若
明詔奬拔者當在玆矣臣曩稽圖
===
報塞或可藉手萬一敢不甚
幸然臣又悚意大懼焉昔唐
虞敷言擇士尤必明試以功
其法始備堯舜不能以言盡
人且如此今所校士與士之
應乎上者皆文也文則取以
敷陳乎道斯已焉耳若行業
punctuated: 命以來，亦惟與共事之臣，夙夜兢惕，思竭其駑下，仰副上意。及握士所爲文讀之，言若人人殊，類能發抒其所素蓄，以不詭于六經之旨。臣盱衡擊節，不可勝收。庶哉賢士，若明詔奬拔者，當在玆矣！臣曩稽圖報塞，或可藉手萬一，敢不甚幸？然臣又悚意大懼焉。昔唐虞敷言擇士，尤必明試以功，其法始備。堯舜不能以言盡人且如此，今所校士與士之應乎上者皆文也。文則取以敷陳乎道斯已焉耳，若行業
translation_en: … receiving my commission, I have only worked together with my fellow officials in trembling vigilance from dawn till night, striving to exhaust my humble abilities in order to fulfill His Majesty's intentions. When I took up the essays composed by the scholars and read them, although their words differed from person to person, they were generally able to express what they had long cultivated without deviating from the purport of the Six Classics. Looking upon them with raised brows and beating time in admiration, I found more fine pieces than could possibly be gathered in. Truly, the worthy scholars whom the illustrious edict seeks to encourage and select must be right here! That which I previously pondered in seeking to repay my obligation—perhaps through this I may have some small means to fulfill one part in ten thousand; how could I not consider myself most fortunate? Yet at the same time my heart is struck with great trepidation. In antiquity, under Yao and Shun (Tang and Yu), when scholars were selected on the basis of their presented words, they still had to be clearly tested by their actual achievements before the method was complete. If even Yao and Shun could not fully judge men by their words alone, how much more so today, when that by which we examine the scholars and that by which the scholars respond to their superiors consists entirely of literary compositions! Literary composition is taken merely as a means to set forth the Way, and nothing more. As for conduct and achievements…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之脩于家而効于時者能懸
度而逆睹之乎異日脫有行
弗逮言文不適用者爲
盛世累人且羣起而訾詆之主
司者何所逃責邪此〔臣〕所爲
懼者大也已復思之干霄之
木不生步仞之丘明月之珍
===
不産蹄涔之水所植者厚則
材大所毓者深則物奇也南
畿山川秀發自古記之而滙
被
聖化最先且久寔首善之地焉詩
不云乎王國克生維周之楨
則士出其間華與實稱以登
punctuated: 之脩于家而効于時者，能懸度而逆睹之乎？異日脫有行弗逮言、文不適用者，爲盛世累，人且羣起而訾詆之，主司者何所逃責邪？此〔臣〕所爲懼者大也。已復思之，干霄之木，不生步仞之丘；明月之珍，不産蹄涔之水。所植者厚則材大，所毓者深則物奇也。南畿山川秀發，自古記之，而滙被聖化，最先且久，寔首善之地焉。《詩》不云乎：「王國克生，維周之楨。」則士出其間，華與實稱，以登
translation_en: … that is cultivated at home and rendered as service to the age—can one conjecture it from afar and foresee it in advance? Should there in days to come happen to be those whose conduct falls short of their words and whose writings are unsuited for practical use, becoming a blemish upon this flourishing age, people will rise up together to criticize and disparage them; how then could those in charge of the examination escape blame? This is why I am so deeply fearful. Yet upon further reflection, trees that brush the skies do not grow on hillocks a few paces high, and bright-moon pearls are not produced in the puddles left by hoofprints. Where the planting is rich, the timber is great; where the nurturing is deep, the product is extraordinary. That the mountains and rivers of the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nanji) blossom with elegance has been recorded since antiquity; moreover, it has been steeped in the transformative influence of the sages earliest and longest, making it truly the foremost place of excellence. Does not the Book of Odes (Shi) say: "The royal domain is able to bring them forth; they are the pillars of Zhou"? Thus among the scholars emerging from this region, whose literary grace matches their substance and who ascend to…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
名茲錄者豈少哉臣之言必
是之過計而厚望者蓋有所
感矣嘗觀
國朝先達名臣大抵朴茂堅特
若無他技能至發爲論議則
經政宰物即此而在以故德
業獨犖然蓋世云臣每想見
===
其爲人則忻然願爲之執鞭
可謂文有其實者非邪近世
挾鉛槧者流其稱引先王譚
說仁義在所斌然矣而往往
盭于當世之務投之鮮効識
者遂議文之盛實之衰也文
不宜過盛夫所貴文者將華
punctuated: 名茲錄者，豈少哉？臣之言必是之過計而厚望者，蓋有所感矣。嘗觀國朝先達名臣，大抵朴茂堅特，若無他技能，至發爲論議，則經政宰物即此而在，以故德業獨犖然蓋世云。臣每想見其爲人，則忻然願爲之執鞭，可謂文有其實者，非邪？近世挾鉛槧者流，其稱引先王，譚說仁義，在所斌然矣，而往往盭于當世之務，投之鮮効，識者遂議文之盛，實之衰也。文不宜過盛。夫所貴文者，將華
translation_en: … their names on this record be few? That my words necessarily express such excessive concern and high hopes is because I have been moved by certain reflections. I have observed that the eminent predecessors and renowned ministers of our reigning dynasty were, on the whole, unadorned, substantial, steadfast, and independent, as though they possessed no other special skills; yet when they expressed themselves in deliberation and discussion, the ordering of governance and the management of affairs were right there within them. For this reason, their moral achievement and statesmanship stood out brilliantly, unmatched in their age. Whenever I envision the kind of men they were, I would gladly hold the whip in their service. Could they not be called men whose literary expression possessed true substance? In recent times, the sort who carry writing brush and tablet cite the former kings and discourse on benevolence and righteousness with resplendent refinement everywhere; yet they are often at odds with the practical affairs of the present age, and when entrusted with tasks, they rarely achieve results. Men of discernment consequently argue that the flourishing of literary refinement marks the decline of substance. Literary refinement ought not to flourish excessively. Now, what is valued in literary refinement is that blossom…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
實竝茂以用世而不爲徒盛
臣所忻慕於先達者是矣若
一于文而無益世用直刻脂
鏤氷者等耳
朝廷待士之厚及士所平時稱
說者意安在也而若此則奚
取于士哉今海內文日盛而
===
南畿尤勝諸士以文舉矣尚
砥行竪業求濟實用以無忝
前聞矣乎況
主上茂齡登阼日明習
國事方
寤寐眞賢爲
新政助而諸士尤四方攸式宜褎
punctuated: 實竝茂，以用世而不爲徒盛，臣所忻慕於先達者是矣。若一于文而無益世用，直刻脂鏤氷者等耳。朝廷待士之厚，及士所平時稱說者，意安在也？而若此，則奚取于士哉？今海內文日盛，而南畿尤勝。諸士以文舉矣，尚砥行竪業，求濟實用，以無忝前聞矣乎！況主上茂齡登阼，日明習國事，方寤寐眞賢，爲新政助。而諸士尤四方攸式，宜褎
translation_en: …and substance flourish together so as to be of use to the world, rather than being merely luxuriant in vain. This is what your servant so joyfully admires in those illustrious predecessors. If one is devoted solely to literary style without benefiting practical use in the world, one is simply no different from someone carving grease or engraving ice. Where, then, would lie the meaning of the Court's generous treatment of scholars, and of what scholars themselves ordinarily profess and discuss? And if they are like this, what would be the point of selecting scholars at all? Today, literary refinement grows daily more flourishing throughout the empire, and the Southern Metropolitan Area (Nanji) excels above all. Now that you scholars have been recommended through your literary compositions, should you not whet your conduct and establish your achievements, seeking to fulfill practical application so as not to bring shame upon the renowned predecessors of the past? Moreover, His Majesty the Sovereign has ascended the throne at a flourishing young age and daily grows more clear-sighted and versed in affairs of state; right now, waking and sleeping, he longs for true worthies to assist in his new administration. And since you scholars are especially those whom the four quarters take as a model, and who ought to stand at the…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
然以興者敢以是望之願諸
士無忘斯言務期實用也務
實者豈必改習故業卽今所
言持以効之他日言孝子忠
臣實竭力致身言仁人貞士
實能愛能守是今日之文廼
先資以成信者耳諸士勉焉
使後閱玆錄者指其名而稱
之曰東南之才不徒以文盛
===
則無負
聖化而增美山川矣顧不重歟嗟
乎士之未遇常患不用旣用
矣人益求其所以用則可患
者尤大焉夫求而得臣與有
punctuated: 然以興者，敢以是望之。願諸士無忘斯言，務期實用也。務實者，豈必改習故業？卽今所言，持以効之他日：言孝子忠臣，實竭力致身；言仁人貞士，實能愛能守。是今日之文，廼先資以成信者耳。諸士勉焉，使後閱玆錄者指其名而稱之曰：「東南之才，不徒以文盛。」則無負聖化，而增美山川矣，顧不重歟？嗟乎！士之未遇，常患不用；旣用矣，人益求其所以用，則可患者尤大焉。夫求而得，臣與有
translation_en: … rise up prominently at the forefront; I venture to hope this of them. I wish that you scholars not forget these words, and strive to achieve practical utility. For one who strives for substance, why must he alter his former studies? Simply take what you have spoken of today, hold fast to it, and put it into effect on a future day: when you speak of filial sons and loyal ministers, truly exhaust your strength and devote your lives; when you speak of benevolent men and upright scholars, truly be able to love others and hold fast to your integrity. Thus the writings of today are simply the advance pledge by which you establish future trust. Exert yourselves, scholars, so that those who later read this record will point to your names and praise them, saying, "The talents of the Southeast flourish not merely in literary writing!" Then you will not fail the sacred transforming influence of the throne, and will add beauty to the mountains and rivers—is this not weighty indeed? Alas! Before a scholar meets with opportunity, he constantly worries about not being employed; once he is employed, others increasingly demand of him that by which he is worthy of employment, and then what is to be worried about is even greater. Now if they demand this and find it in you, I too shall share in…

title: 萬曆四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
榮否則不惟士自貽厥愚而
臣之大懼終不可釋敢以自
幸故令于諸士始進臣惓惓
以文實之辨叙論于末冀有
所先入諸士勿謂臣言無亦
虛文也哉
右春坊右賛善兼翰林院檢
討陳思育謹序
punctuated:
榮；否則，不惟士自貽厥愚，而臣之大懼終不可釋，敢以自幸？故令于諸士始進，臣惓惓以文實之辨叙論于末，冀有所先入。諸士勿謂臣言無亦虛文也哉！
右春坊右賛善兼翰林院檢討陳思育謹序。
translation_en:
… share in the honor; otherwise, not only will the scholars bring folly upon themselves, but your servant's great dread will ultimately never be relieved—how could I dare to consider myself fortunate? Therefore, at this moment[?] when the scholars are first advancing into office, your servant earnestly sets forth this discussion distinguishing between literary flourish and substantial reality at the end of the record, hoping that it may take root in their minds first. May the scholars not say that your servant's words are, after all, mere empty rhetoric!

Respectfully prefaced by Chen Siyu 陳思育, Right Admonisher of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy.
